The instrument cluster outputs a reference voltage to the turn signal indicator switch. When the switch i in the central off position, the voltage flows through 3 resistors which are connected in series and back to the instrument cluster which monitors the signal and determines the turn signal indicators are of. This iformation is broadcast on the medium speed CAN bus to the CJB .

When the switch is operated in the LH turn signal indicator position, the reference voltage from the instrument cluster is routed via 1 of the resistors. The returned signal voltage is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on themedium speed CN bus to the The activates the applicable turn signal icators until  rives an off messae from the instrument cluster.

When the switch is operated in the RH turn signal indicator position, the reference voltage from the instrument cluster is routed via 2 of the resistors. The returned signal voltage is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CN bus t the The  activates the applicale tun signal inicators until i ives anoff messae from the instrument cluster.

The instrument cluster outputs  reference voltages to the rotary lighting control switch; one feed being supplied to the light selection function of the switch and the second feed being supplied to the autolamp exit delay function. The switch position is determined by instrument cluster by the change in returned signal voltage which is routed through up to 4 resistors in series depending on' the selection made.

When thelighting control switch i in the offposition, the rference voltageflws through  of theresistors.The rturned signal voltage is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the  that no lghting selection is made. The reference voltage to the autolamp exit delay witch is routed through 4 resistors which is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the C that autolamp or exit delay has not been selected.

When the lighting control switch is in the sidelamp position, the reference voltage flows through 2 of the resistors.The returned signal voltage is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the CB to activate the sidelamps. The reference voltage to the autolamp exit delay switch is routed through 4 resistors which is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the C that autolamp or exit delay has ñot been selected.

When the lighting control switch is in the headlamp position, the reference voltage flows through  of the resistors. The returned signal voltage is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the CB to activate the headamps. The reference voltage to the autolamp exit delay switch is routed through 4 resistors which i detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medum speed CAN bus to the  that utolamp or exit delay has not been selected.

When the lighting control switch is in the autolamp position, the reference voltage flows through 4 of the resistors. The returned signal voltage is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the CB to activate the autolamp function. The reference voltage to the autolamp exit delay switch i routed through 4 resistors which is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the  that autolamp has been selected.

When the lighting control switch i in any of the autolamp exit delay position, the lighting control switch reference voltage flows through 4 of the resistors. The returned signal voltage is detected by the instrument cluster which outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the CJB that autolamps has been selected.

Depending on the selected position, the reference voltage to the autolamp exit delay switch is routed through 3, 2 or 1 resistors which is detected by the instrument cluster. The cluster outputs a message on the medium speed CAN bus to the CJB that autolamp exit delay period has been selected at 30, 60 or 120 seconds respectively.

CAUTIoON: Steering gear boots must be handled carefull to avoid damage. Use new clamps when instaling steering gear boots. Inspect the boots for cuts, deterioration, twisting or distortion. Check the steering gear boots to make sure they are tight. Install new boots or clamps as required

NOTE: The following steps must be carried out with power steering assistance (with the engine running):

With the wheels in the straight ahead position, gently turn the steering wheel to the left and the right to check for free play

Free play should be between 0 and 6 mm (0 and 0.24 in) at the steering wheel rim. If the free play exceeds this limit, either the balljoints are worn (Refer to videos shown on SSM41218 for guidance for the procedure to check for worn Outer Bl Joints or Inner Ball Joints), or the lower steering column jonts are worn (REFER to: Section 211-04 Steering Column/Diagnosis and Testing/Steering Column/Pinpoint Tests/ Noise Specific Diagnostics (Clonk/Column Knock Check For Clok/Column Knock Noise From Lower Steering Column Shaft, or the backash of the steering gear is excessive

cAuTIoN: Do NoT attempt to adjust the steering gear yoke. Failure to follow this instruction wil invalidate the steering gear warranty

The backlash of the steering gear cannot be adjusted, installnew steering gear if excessive backlash is diagnosed after checking for worn ball joints and lower steering column joints

Grasp the steering whee firmly and attempt to move it laterally, both up and down and to the left and the right (without turning the wheel), to check for column bearing wear

The FRPT sensor provides the ECM with a continuous signal of fuel rail pressure.The FRPT sensor is installed in the rear of the right fuel rail. The FRPT sensor is screwed into a threaded boss in the fuel rail.

The FRPT sensor contains a steel diaphragm fitted with strain gages, which are incorporated into a Wheatstone bridge.The output from the Wheatstone bridge is processed by the ECM to determine a pressure value.

Two fuel level sensors are installed in either side of the sadde tank. One is mounted on the fuel pump module and is known asfel level sensor'A', the ther  mounte on the arrier in the left side of the fuel tank and iow as fuel level sensor The sensors are float operated APS(magneti passive poition sensor which provide a variale resistance to ground for the output to the fuel level gaugein the instrument cluster.The sensor is sealed from the fuel preventing contamination of the contacts, icreasing reliaility The fuel level sensors are conected to the externallectrical coector  the flange via the connector on the underside of the fuel pump module flange.

The sensor comprises a series of  film resistors mounted in an arc on a ceramic surface. The resistors are wired in series with individual contacts. A soft magnetic foil with 51 flexible contacts is mounted a small distance above the film resistors. A magnet, located below the ceramic surface, is attached to the sender unit float arm. As the float arm moves, the magnet folows the same arc as the film resistors. The magnet pull the flexible contacts onto the opposite film resistor contacts forming an electrical circuit.

![](images/_MISSING_7c5e069b923620d240e49d66c84627cfa51fcc270b9d344820114103f8d8257c.jpg)

E44504   
![](images/_MISSING_453eba9b2cec5d296441e1fa36d533ff4dc844caeca0174da91fb3351b392c31.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_5d6d3f329e53da2443a618d849ab5574cbb634c51228eb64cc60cf2a6cff9d62.jpg)

The fim resistors are arranged in a linear arc with resistance ranging from 51.2 to 992.11 hms. The electrical output sigal is proportional to the amount of fuel in the tank and the position of the float arm.The measured resistance is processed by the instrument cluster to implement an anti-slosh function. This monitors the signal and updates the fuel gauge pointer position at regular intervals, preventing constant pointer movement caused by fuel movement in the tank due to conering o braking.

A warning lamp is incorporated in the instrument cluster and iluminates when the fuel level is low.

The fuel level sensor signal is converted into a CAN (controlle area network) message by the instrument cluster as a direct interpretation of the ful tank contents in liters. The M uses the CAN message to store aditional OBD on-board danosti) 'P' Codes for misfire detection when the fuel level is below a predetermined capacity.

The fuel LP sensor suppies a pressure signal to the EM to enable closed loop control of the fuel pump. The fuel LP sensor is installed in a manifold in the fuel delivery line on the top of the fuel pump module.

The manifold is attached to a bracket which is located above the fuel pump module flange, on the right side of the fuel tank. The manifold has three conections; one is unused and blanked, the second receives the fuel supply from the fuel pump and the third diects the fuel from the fuel pump to the fuel delivery line to theengine.The sensor cated n the manifoland measures the fuel pressure being supplied from the fuel pump before it is delivered to the engine.

The front section has a flared end which mates with a corresponding feature on the turbocharger. The joint is secured together using a 'V' band clamp sealed with a gasket.

The flange is formed on a fabricated outlet elow which in turn is welded to the flexible joint. On all vehicles the elbow incoportes a threaded boss which provides the location for the HO2S. On vehicles with a DPF, a second boss provides for the fitment of an exhaust gas temperature sensor. The flexible joint i welded to the body of the catalytic converter.A curved connecting pipe is welded to the catalytic converter. On vehicles with a DPF fitted, the cuved pipe incoporates a threaded boss which provides for the fitment of a second exhaust gas temperature sensor.

The curved pipe from the catalytic converter has a flange which mates with a flange on the DPF. The flanges are sealed with a metal gasket and secured with three studs and nuts.The DPF outlet has a short connecting pipe which mates with the connectin pipe of the rear silencer system and is secured with 'Torca'clamp joint. Two mounting rubbers are located near to the catalyst and attach to a body hanger bracket mounted on the front subframe. Another rubber mounting is attached to the DPF outlet pipe near the clamp joint.

The rear section has long connecting pipe section which mates with the outlet pipe from the catalyst or DPFand is secure with a clamp joint. The pipe section i routed along the underside of the vehicle and connects into the center of the rear muffler.

The rear mufler is a fabricated unit with a capacity of 8.liters.The muffer contains perforated baffles and tubes which are tuned to reduce noise and enhance exhaust sound quality as the exhaust gases passthrough the silencer. Active regeneration starts when the particulate loading of the DPF reaches a threshold as monitored or determined by the DPF control software. The threshold calculation is based on driving style, distance travelled and back pressure signals fron the differential pressure sensor.

Active regeneration gnerall occurs every 250 miles (400 km) although this is dependant on how the vehicle is driven. For example, i the veicleis driven at low loads i uran traffiregulay, active rgeeration wilccur more often. Thi is due to the rapid build-up of partiulates in the DPF than if the vehicle is driven at high speeds when passve regeneration will have occurred.

The DPF software incoporates a mileage trigger which is used as back-up for active regeneration. If active regeneration has not been initiated by a back pressure signal from the differential pressure sensor regeneration is requested based on distance travelled.

Active regeneration of the DPFis commenced when the temperature of the DPF is increased to the combustion temperatur ofthe particles.The DPF temperature iaised by ireasing the exhaust as temperature.Thisis achieved by introducing post-injection of fuel after the pilot and main fuél injections have occurred.

It is determined by the DPF software monitoring the signals from the two DPF temperature sensors to establish the tmperature of the DPF.Depending on the DPF temperature, the DPF software requests the ECM (engine control module t oerform either one or two post-injections of fuel:

The first post-injection of fuel retards combustion inside the cylinder which increases the temperature of the exhaust gas. The second post-injection of fuel is ijected late in the power stroke cycle. The fuel partly combusts in the cylinder, but some unburnt fuel also passes into the exhaust where it creates an exothermic event within the catalytic converter, further increasing the temperature of the DPF.

The active regeneration process takes up to 20 minutes to complete. The first phase increases the DPF temperature to 00 (932.The seond phase further icreases the DPF temperature to 600 (1112F) which is the optimum temperature for particle combustion. This temperature is then maintained for 15-20 minutes to ensure complete oxidation of the particles within the DPF. The oxidation process converts the carbon particles to carbon dioxide.

The active regeneration temperature of the DPF is closely monitored by the DPFsoftware to maintain a target temperature of00at te FTe mpeatre cr eSurest te mpears notecehe i limits of the turbocharger and the catalytic converter. The turbocharger inlet temperature must not exceed 830° (1526°F) and the catalytic converter brick temperature must not exceed 800° (1472°F) and the exit temperature must remain below 875 (1382°).

During the active regeneration process the following ECM controlled events occur:

The turbocharger is maintained in the fully open position. This minimizes heat transmission from the exhaust gas to the turbocharger and reduces the rate of exhaust gas flow allowing optimum heating of the DPF. If the driver demands an increase in engine torque, the turbocharger will respond by closing the vanes as necessary. The throttle is closed as this assists in increasing the exhaust gas temperature and reduces the rate of exhaust gas flow which has the effect of reducing the time for the DPF to reach the optimum temperature. The EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) valve is closed. The use of EGR decreases the exhaust gas temperature and therefore prevents the optimum DPF temperature being achieved."

There are threevariants of speed control available; a standard speed control system, an adaptive speed control system and an Automatic Speed Limiter (ASL) system.

The standard speed control system maintains a set speed selected by the driver until operation is suspended or cancelled by a further input from the driver and is controlled by the Engine Control Module (ECM).

The adaptive speed control system system includes the same functionality as the standard system, but also has the ability to:

Reduce vehicle speed, to less than the set speed, in order to maintain a selected time gap behind a slower moving vehiclle   
Accelerate the vehicle back to the set speed, once the way ahead is clear, after reducing the set speed because of a slower moving vehicle   
Alert the driver when the vehicle comes within a given time gap of a slower moving vehicle (forward alert feature).

The ASL system restricts the vehicle speed to an adjustable preset maximum, and wil prevent the vehicle exceeding that speed.

The Inteligent Stop/Start system is controlled by the ECM using CAN (controller area network) messages and signals from other system components and modules to determine the correct conditions for system operation.

The Inteligent Stop/Start system detects when it is appropriate to stop and start the engine.

Before the engine is stopped, the following parameters must be detected:

The vehicle must be stopped from a speed greater than 4 km/h (2.5 mph) Suffiient brake pressure must be applied to the brake pedal to ensure the vehicle is stationary OR The vehicle must be stationary and P or N selected on the TCS (transmission control switch) .

Before the engine is restarted, the following parameters must be detected:

Drive 'D' or Sport 'S' selected on the TCS and the brake pedal is released   
•The accelerator pedal is pressed ECM detects a signal from the APP (accelerator pedal position)   
A steering wheel paddle switch is operated to select a gear   
Reverse 'R' is selected on the TCS   
Climate control system demand increases (signal from the ATC (automatic temperature control) The vehicle speed exceeds approximately 1 km/h (0.5 mph) Battery and/or secondary battery charge becomes low (signal from the DBM)   
Brake vacuum has been reduced from repeated use of pedal with engine not running (detected by ECM from the brake vacuum sensor)   
ECO stop/Start is deactivated using ECO switch in the Integrated Control Panel (ICP).

The following conditions will prevent an ECO stop:

A steering wheel paddle switch has been used to select a gear The external ambient temperature is less than 0°C (32°F) (detected by ECM from ambient air temperature sensor) The external ambient temperature is more than 40°C (104°F) (detected by ECM from ambient air temperature sensor) The engine has not reached its optimum operating temperature (detected by ECM from ECT (engine coolant temperature) sensor) The driver door is opened (detected by CJB (central junction box) from door ajar switch) The driver safety belt is not fastened (detected by RCM (restraints control module) from driver front buckle switch) The climate control system requires the engine to be running, for example; windshield demist selected The primary and/or secondary battery charge is low (signal from the DBM) The hood is open (detected by CJB from hood ajar switch) ECO stop/start is deactivated using the ECO switch in the ICP.

The battery is used for the engine Stop/Start. The secondary battery is switched by the DM to maintain the car systems, for example, audio, limate or lghts, which are then unaffected by the ngine restart.For addtional iformation, referto: (414-01 Battery, Mounting and Cables)

Battery and Cables (Description and Operation), Battery and Cables (Description and Operation), Battery and Cables (Description and Operation). Stop/Start Strategy

The TSS motor and the Inteligent Stop/Start system allows the vehicle engine to be restarted during an engine stop cycle, allowing the driver to proceed before the engine comes to a complete stop. This would not be possible without the SS motor

The feature of the motor and the pinion gear being operated individuall allows meshing ofthe pinion gear with the drive plate ring gear, even if the engine is still operating. This allows seamless Stop/Start without hesitation.

Operation of the transmission is controlled by the TM (transmission control module)  which electrically activates various solenoids to control the transmisson gear selection. The sequence of solenoid activation is based on programmed information in the M memory and physical tranmission operating conditions such as vehicle speed, throtle position, engine load and selector lever position.

All gear shift from 1st to 8th and 8th to 1st are known as 'verlap'shifts. Overlap shifts are during a gear shift and one clutch must remain capable of transmitting torque at a reduced main pressure until the other clutch is ready to accept the torque.

The shift elements, clutches and brakes are actuated hydraulicall. Fluid pressure is applied to the required clutch and/or brake, pressig the plates together and allwing drive to be transmitted through the plates.The purpose of the shift lement is to perform power-on shifts with no interruption to traction and smooth transition between gear ratios.

The MIL (malfunction indicator lamp) is located in the tachometer ofthe instrument cluster. Transmission related faults which may affect the vehicle emissions wil illuminate the MIL .

The TCC (torque converter clutch) is hydraulically controlled by an Electronic Pressure Regulating Solenoid (EPRS) , which is controlled by the TCM . This allows the torque converter to have three states of operation as follows:

Fully engaged   
Controlled slip variable engagement Fully disengaged. The torque converter pressure valve reduces system pressure and guarantees the pressure needed for the torque converter.   
It also limits the maximum torque converter pressure, to prevent the torque converter from expanding.

The solenoid valve is operated by PW (pulse width modulation) signals from the TM to give ful, partial or no lock-up of the torque converter.

The lock-up clutch is a hydro-mechanical device which eliminates torque converter slip, improving fuel consumption. The engagement and disengagement is controlled by the TM to allow a certain amount of controlled 'slip'. This allows a small dfference in the rtational speeds of the impeller and the turbie which result in improved shift qulity. The lock-up clutch comprises a piston and a clutch friction plate.

In the unlocked condition, the oil pressure supplied to the piston chamber is reduced and the pressure in the turbine chamber is allowed to push the piston back. In this condition the clutch plate are released and torque converter lip is permitted.

In the locked condition, the TCC spool valves are actuated by the EPRS. Pressurized fluid is directed into the lock-up clutch piston. The piston moves with the pressure and pushes the clutch plates together. As the pressure increases, the friction between the clutch plates increases, finall resulting in fullock-up of the clutch plates. In this condition there is direct mechanical drive from the engine crankshaft to the transmission planetary gear train.

The Transmission Ide Control (T) feature is a standstil decoupling feature new for the 8 speed transmission. When the vehicle comes t a standstil i Drive with the brakes applied), the converter is disconnected from the driveline so that only a slight residual load remains. This further reduces fuel consumption. Decoupling is by actuating clutch B in the transmission, and is dependent on load and output speed.

![](images/_MISSING_21cdcba8e2c5461b0b715020a2e5a5825c6df0f29b60e583e443ecb42f561e9a.jpg)

A shift control solenoid  (Magnetic Valve 1 is located in the valve block. The solenoid is controlled by the TCM and converts electrical signals into hýdraulic control signals to control clutch application.

The shift control solenoid is an open/closed, on/offsolenoid which is controlled by the TM switching the solenoid to earth. The TCM also supplies power to the solenoid. The TM energises the solenoid in a programmed seqence for clutch appliation for gear ratio changes and shift control.

The resistance of the solenoid coil winding for solenoid is between 10 to 11 Ohms at 20 °C (68 °F).

A control solenoid MV  (Magnetic Valve 2is located in the valve block. The solenoid is controlled by the TM and convert electrical signals into hydraulic control signals to control the electronic park lock function

The control solenoid is an on/off solenoid which is controlled by the TCM by switching the solenoid to earth.

When the park position is deselected, control solenoid M resets the parking lock valve in the Mechatronic valve block. This iachieved by the M providing the ground for the solenoid which is energized, releasing the claws from retaining the park lock piston. Main fluid pressure acting on the parking lock piston, pushes the piston back to release the lock.

When the park position i selected, control solenoid  is deenergized. The fluid pressure at the parking lock cylinder piston is vented and the mechanical interlock of the piston is opened. A pre-tensioned torsion spring at the park lock disc pull the piston into the"park" position where the piston engages with the control solenoid claws and is locked in the park position. An emergency release wire cable can be used to release the parking lock manually if an electrical failure occurs.

The resistance of the solenoid coil winding for solenoid is 25 Ohms at 20 °C (68 °F).

When the nutral "" position i selectedand the engine is turned off the fluid pressure at the park lock clinder piston is released.The current supply to the control solenoid remains. The park lock cylinder piston is stil held in the unlocked position by the spring force acting on the park lock disc, preventing the park lock plate from engaging the parking lock. This allws the vehicle to be oved when the engine is not runing for  short time. Should the battery voltage fal below the level required to maintain the solenoid in the energized condition, the park lock will be engaged.

The ZF 8HP70 transmission is an electronical controlled, hydraulically operated, 8 speed automatic unit. The hydraulic and electronic control elements of the transmission, iluding the M (transmissioncontrol module)  are incorporated n a single unit located inside the transmission and is known as 'Mechatronic'.

The ZF 8HP70 transmission has the following features:

Designed to be maintenance free   
Transmission fluid is 'fill for life'   
The torque converter features a controlled slip feature with electronical regulated control of lock-up, creating a smooth transition to the fully locked condition   
Shift programs controlled by the TCM   
ASIS (adaptive shift strategy), to provide continuous adaptation of shift changes to suit the driving style of the driver, which can 'vary from sporting to economical   
Connected to the ECM (engine control module) via the high speed CAN (controller area network) bus for   
communications   
Default mode if major faults occur   
Diagnostics available from the TCM via the high speed CAN bus.

The higher fuel efficiency of the ZF 8HP70 automatic transmission is mainly due to the follwing modifications:

a wider ratio spread and more gears for better adaptation to ideal engine operating points significantly reduced drag torque in the shift elements (only two open shift elements per gear) use of a more efficient ATF (automatic transmission fluid pump (double-stroke vane pump) Decoupling of the transmission when the vehicle is at standstill   
improved torsion damping in the converter.

The transmission selections are made using the rotary JaguarDrive TCs (transmission control switch) in the floor console. Refer to: External Controls (307-05B Automatic Transmission/Transaxle External Controls - GTDi 2.0L Petrol/TD4 2.2L Diesel/TDV6 3.0L Diesel /V6 S/C 3.0L Petrol, Description and Operation).

The DW12 engine features stop/start technology. To complement this, the 8 speed transmisson is fited with a hydraulic impulse storage device to ensure ATF i available to the shift elements as quickly as possible when the engine is started.

Operation of the transmission is controlled by the TM (transmission control module)  which electrically activates various solenoids to control the transmission gear selection. The sequence of solenoid activation is based on programmed information ithe M memory and physical transmission operating conditions such as vehicle speed, throtte position, engine load and TCS (transmission control switch) position.

All gear shifts from 1st to 8th and 8th to 1st are known as 'verlap'shifts. Overlap shifts are during a gear shift and one cutch must remain capable of transmiting torque at a reduced main pressure until the other clutch is ready to accept the torque.

Engine torque is transferred, via operation of single or combinations of clutches to the4 planetary gear trains. All gear trains are controlled by reactionary inputs from brake clutches to produce the 8 forward gears and 1 reverse gear. The ratios are as follows:

![](images/_MISSING_fc801e364d8680f9ef7b08180b1caf222dfeb978da8529aca1da0258e1ce31e5.jpg)

The shift elements, clutches and brakes are actuated hydraulical. Fluid pressure is applied to the required clutch and/or brake,pressig the plates together and allwing drive to be transmitted through the plates.The purpose of the shift elements is to perform power-on shifts with no interruption to traction and smooth transition between gear ratios.

The TCC (torque converter clutch) is hydrauliclly controlled by an Electronic Pressure Regulating Solenoid (EPRS) , which is controlled by the TCM . This allows the torque converter to have three states of operation as follows:

Fully engaged   
Controlled slip variable engagement Fully disengaged.

The torque converter pressure valve reduces system pressure and guarantees the pressure needed for the torque converter It also limits the maximum torque converter pressure, to prevent the torque converter from expanding.

The EPRS is operated by PWM (pulse width modulation) signals from the M to give ful, partial or no lock-up of the torqu converter.

The lock-up clutch is a hydro-mechanical device which eliminates torque converter slip, improving fuel consumption. The engagement and disengagement is controlled by the TM to allow a certain amount of controlled 'slip'. This allows a small dfference in the rtational speeds of the impeller and the turbie which result in improved shift qulity. The lock-up clutch comprises a piston and a clutch friction plate.

In the unlocked condition, the oil pressure supplied to the piston chamber i reduced and the pressure in the turbine chamber is llowed to push the piston back. In this condition the clutch plate are released and torque converter slip is permitted.

In the locked condition, the TCC spool valves are actuated by the EPRS. PressurizedATF is directed into the lock-up clutch piston. The piston moves with the pressure and pushes the clutch plates together. As the pressure increases, the friction between the clutch plates increases, finall resulting in fullock-up of the clutch plates. I this condition there is direct mechanical drive from the engine crankshaft to the transmission planetary gear train.

The Transmission dle Control (T feature is a standstilldecoupling feature for the 8 speed transmission. When the vehicle comes to a standstillin Drive with the brakes applied), the converter is disconected from the driveline so that only a slight residual load remains. This further reduces fuel consumption. Decoupling is by actuating clutch  in the transmission, and is dependent on load and output speed.

![](images/_MISSING_81eb9628ca2d0df30ea145b9ee2a53c64e47ca33ec656f7ac0161ea4212eabd7.jpg)

A shift control solenoid  (Magnetic Valve 1 is located in the valve block. The solenoid is controlled by the TCM and converts electrical signals into hýdraulic control signals to control clutch application.

The shift control solenoid is an open/closed, on/offsolenoid which is controlled by the TM switching the solenoid to earth. The TCM also supplies power to the solenoid. The TM energises the solenoid in a programmed seqence for clutch appliation for gear ratio changes and shift control.

The resistance of the solenoid coil winding for solenoid is between 10 to 11 Ohms at 20 °C (68 °F).

The ZF 8HP70 transmission is an electronically controlled, hydraulicallyoperated, 8 speed automatic unit. The hydraulic and electronic control elements of the transmission, including the M (transmission control module) , are incorporated in a single unit located inside the transmission and is known as 'Mechatronic'.

The ZF 8HP70 transmission has the following features:

Designed to be maintenance free   
Automatic Transmission Fluid (ATF) is fil for life'   
The torque converter features a controlled slip feature with electronicall regulated control of lock-up, creating a smooth transition to the fuly locked condition   
Shift programs controlled by the TCM   
ASIS adaptive shift strategy), to provide continuous adaptation of shift changes to suit the driving style of the driver, which can vary from sporting to economical   
Connected to the ECM (engine control module) via the high speed CAN (controller area network) bus for   
communications   
Default mode if major faults occur   
Diagnostics available from the TCM via the high speed CAN bus.

The higher fuel efficiency of the ZF 8HP70 automatic transmission is mainly due to the follwing modifications:

A wider ratio spread and more gears for better adaptation to ideal engine operating points Significantly reduced drag torque in the shift elements (only two open shift elements per gear) Use of a more efficient ATF (automatic transmission fluid) pump (double-stroke vane pump) Decoupling of the transmission when the vehicle is at standstill   
Improved torsion damping in the converter.

The transmission selections are made using the rotary JaguarDrive Ts (transmission control switch) in the floor console. Refer to: External Controls (307-05A Automatic Tranmission/Transaxle External Controls - V8 5.0L Petrol/V8 S/ 5.0L Petro Diagnosis and Testing).

The 3.0L V6 S/ engine features stop/start technology on some models. To complement this, the 8 speed transmission, on vehicles with stop/start echnology, is fited with a Hydraulic mpulse Storage (HIS) device to ensure AT i vilable to the shift elements as quickly as possible when the engine is started.

Two versions of the 8HP70 transmission are available; one version is for RWD (rear wheel drive) vehicles and the second i for AWD (all-wheel drive) vehicles. The transmission internals of both transmissions are similar.

The TCS is a rotary selector installed in the top of the TS module. The TS module is located in the floor console and also controls the vehicle optimization functions on the vehicle. Refer to: Ride and Handling Optimization (204-06 Ride and Handling Optimization, Description and Operation) / Anti-Lock Control - Stability Assist (206-09 Anti-Lock Control - Stability Assist, Description and Operation).

By selecting P, R, N, D or S on the TCS, the transmission functions as any conventional automatic unit.

Rotation of theS allows the selection of P, R, N and D. By depressing the S and rotating clockwise from the D position,S mode can be selected. The TCS is a full electronic rotary transmission selector with no mechanical connection to the transmission.

The TCS rises from the TS module once the engine is running. When the engine is stopped with the TS in any position other than  i rract into theSmodule agin the  i ipositn  whentheegin isstpped,  emins itheised position for up to 10 minutes, for use in adrive through car wash for example. After 0 minutes the selector automatically retracts into the S module.The selector als retracts i P isselected within the 10 minute periodor the vehicle i locked.

If the  does not rise fom the console when the engine is started but lectrical power is supplied to the s, the retracted TCS canstil be rtated to makeselections. If eletrical power to the S is lost, theS willnot rise from the floor console when the engine is started and the retracted TCS will not rotate.

The TCS contains an internal interlock solenoid to prevent the TS from being rotated when the engine is not running.

The engine can be stopped with the S in any position. Once the engine is stopped the selector will automaticall reset to the  position and the transmission park lock wil be engaged, except i the selector is moved to the ' position hen the engine is stopped.

### Showroom Representative Responsibilities


he active antitheft system is available with three different levels of vehicle protection depending on market specifiction:

Hinged panel sensing Hinged panel and intrusion sensing Hinged panel, intrusion and inclination sensing.

The system is controlled by software in the CJB and RJB and indicates a trigger condition:

Visually, using the direction indicators, and Audibly, using the vehicle horn and either a passive or active sounder to indicate a trigger condition.

The passive sounder takes the form of an anti-theft disc horn located at the rear of the engine compartment on the LH side.   
The active sounder takes the form of a battery backed sounder located in the same position.

Depending on market specification, the battery backed sounder may be fitted with an inclination sensor. Both types of batery baked sounder are visul identical and can only be identified by their part number. Both are also inteligent units, and communicate to the CJB over a LIN (local interconnect network) bus connection.

Monitoring of the hinged panels is carried out using switches located in each door latch assembly, the engine-compartment-lic latch assembly, and the luggage-compartment-lid latch assembly. The condition of the switches is monitored by the CB.

Monitoring of front door lock status is carried out using switches located in the door latch mechanisms. The condition of the switches is monitored by the front door modules and transmitted to the CB over the medium speed CAN (controller area network) bus.

Monitoring of the cabin interior is carred out using an intrusion detection module mounted behind the roof console.The intrusion detection module comprises an ultrasonic sound wave sensor to determine if there is movement within the cabin.

Information from the intrusion detection module is communicated to the CJB over a LIN bus connection.

Operation of the battery backed sounder is controlled by the C on the LIN bus. The sounder is also connected with a permanent battery supply via the C.An integral, rechargeable battey powers the sounder if the battey power supply from the CJB is interrupted.

Dependant on vehicle, a incitation sensor is incorporated into the batery backed sounder, to monitor vehicle atitude, see Inclination Sensor.

For a detailed description of the anti-theft - passive system, refer to the relevant description and operation sections in the workshop manual. REFER to: (419-01B Anti-Theft - Passive)

Anti-Theft - Passive (Description and Operation), Anti-Theft - Passive (Description and Operation), Anti-Theft - Passive (Description and Operation).

The best method to cofirm the corect operation of the passve antitheft system is to check the LED (located in the center of the instrument panel. The LED should iluminate solid for 3 seconds, when the ignition status is set to ON, and then extinguish. This validates all passve anti-theft system functions i.e. the key transponder matches a stored key code, the chllenge/response sequence between the respective modules was succesful resulting in the engine management system being enabled)

For the various passive antitheft system modes/aults listed in the table, the instrument cluster will store a DT and indicate this to the customer during the detection period defined in the 'when logged' column, by iluminating the indicator as described for 60 seconds and then flashing the LED 10 times as appropriate.The indication wil stop mmediately the ignition status is set to OFF any time during the fault indication sequence. Up to 4 DTCs could be stored per key read sequence (1-10 read attempts). No DTs will be stored until ll etry attempts are complete. Only the highest priority fault code will be flashed

To determine the fault code from the LED The LED willfah illy ten times with . seconds between.The LED will emain OFF for 2.5 seconds then flash a number of times with 0.5 seconds between (the number of times the LED flashes represents the first digit of the code, the LE wil remain FF for. seond then flash a number of times with 1. seconds between (the number of times the LED flashes represents the second digit of the code)

The passve anti-theft system LED will be commanded on as shown under indication'. Normal passive anti-theft system operations are complete within 40ms of the ignition switch transition from OFFto ON or START, worst case for engine control module communication problems will be lessthan 2 seconds. If passve anti-theft system is not complete during the 2 seconds the engine control module wil terminate passive anti-theft system and await the next ignition ON or START event. Passive anti-theft system faults will be indicated via the LED as soon as possible and wil terminate the LED prove out. At iitionOfFll previous flashing will ease and the perimeter antitheft system will control the LED when the veicle is locked and armed

The BS control module is located on the primary battery negative  terminal. The module is located on the battery post and is clamped to the post with a bolt and nut.

The primary battry negative ground cable is connected to the BMS control module and is attached to a ground stud on the vehicle body.

The BMS control module is connected into the vehicle wiring harness via a multiplug.The BMS control module receives a 12 power suppy direct from the primary battery positive terminal. A LIN bus connection provides communication between the BMS control module and the уCM for control and monitoring of the primary battery current drain and state of charge.

The BMS control module measures battery current and voltage, which it communicates to ECM .

CAutioN: Due to the self-calibration routine,i is recommended that all power supply diagnostic testing is carried out using the Jaguar approved diagnostic system rather than a digital multimeter.

The BMS control module is able to generate DTC's to help diagnose primary battery or generator power supply issues. These DTC's can be read using the Jaguar approved diaostic system.The Jaguar approved diaostic system can also be used to implement a primary battry and generator self test routine. For additional information, refer to the Diagnosis and Testing section of the workshop manual.

If a fault is detected, the GWM will override the BMS control module.

The BMS control module DTC's can be used to help diagnose battery or generator power supply faults. The DTC's are stored in GWM. The Jaguar approved diagnostic system has a process for an automated power supply diagnostic procedure. The procedure provides a menu driven process to locate a fault in a logical sequence. The procedure uses the capability of the BMS control module and generator L bus controlle functions to provide current flow information and willdetect if the BMS control module or generator are functioning correctly.

Operation of the face level reisters i controlled by the AT module, using LI bus messages t the integral tepper motors.   
The four registers operate together in both the opening and closing phases.

The face level reisters can be selected to run in one of two modes; 'utomatic' or 'always pen' The mode is selected on the climate control screen of the TSD. Refer to: Navigation System (415-01 Information and Entertainment System, Description and Operation).

In the automatic mode, operation of the face level registers is synchronized with the engine START/STOP button. When the engine starts and the blower is on, the ATC module opens the registers. When the engine stops, the ATC module closes the registers.

If a face level register is fouled, when it receives an open or close request, the register concerned makes a number of atempts t reach the requested poition. f the reistersill des not move it lef in the fouled position.The emaining registers will continue to open and close as normal.

The automatic mode is disabled when the limate control system is off The ATC module closes the registers if they are open in the automatic mode and the climate control system is selected off.

When A/ is selected the ATC module maintains the evaporator at an operating temperature that varies with the passenger compartment coling requirements. If the requirement for cooled air decreases, the ATC module raises the evaporator operating temperature by reducing the flow of refrigerant provided by the A/ compressor. The ATC module closely controls the rate of temperature increase to avoid introducing moisture into the passenger compartment.

f the requirement for cooled air increases, the ATC module lowers the evaporator operating temperature by increasing the flow of refrigerant provided by the A/C compressor.

When A/C is of, the compressor current signal supplied by the ATC module holds the A/C compressor solenoid valve in the minimum flow position, effectively switching off the A/C function.

The ATC module incorporates limits for the operating pressure of the refrigerant system. If the system approaches the high pressure limit, the compressor curent signal is progressively reduced until the system pressure decreases. f the system falls below the low pressure limit, the compressor current signal is held at its lowest setting so that the A/ compressor is maintained at its minimum stroke. This avoids depletion of the lubricant from the A/C compressor.

The A/ compressor solenoid valve is integral with the A/ compressor. Operation ofthe solenoid valve is controlled by the ATC module using a hardwired drive current of diffring values.By controling the flow of refrigerant through the compressor, the solenoid valve can control the A/C system pressure and the evaporator operating temperature.

### Humidity and Temperature Sensor


![](images/_MISSING_d7d76055b1d03b3463ad8205ddb9e20f8170ce65b8022f03f4014ac8af220a32.jpg)

he humidity and temperature sensor is installed above the glovebox in the instrument panel. The sensor incorporates:

A NTC thermistor to measure temperature.   
A capacitive sensor element to measure humidity.   
A motor driven fan to draw air through the sensor and over the sensing elements.

The humidity sensor element is built out of a film capacitor on different substrates. The dielectri is a polymer which absorbs or releases water proportional to the relative humidity of the air being drawn through the sensor, and thus changes the capacitance of the capacitor. For protection, the sensor element is contained in a nylon mesh cover.

Humidity within the passenger compartment is controlled by raising and lowering the evaporator temperature. An increase in evaporator temperature increases the moisture content of the air entering the passenger compartment. Lowering the evaporator temperature reduces the moisture content of the air entering the passenger compartment.

The DRL (daytime running lamps) and side lamps are incorporated into the outer part of the headlamp assemblies.   
Refer to: Exterior Lighting (417-01 Exterior Lighting, Description and Operation).

The same LED (light emitingdiodes are used for the two lamp functions, but they iluminate with a higher intensity for DRL operation than for side lamp operation. On Japan vehicles, the DRL function is inoperative.

The DRL operate automatically when a gear i selected after starting the engine. They then remain on until the ignition is switched off, or side lamps or headlamps are selected on.

On NAS vehicles, the DRL also go offif the transmission is selected to P or N and the parking brake is applied.

When a turn signal indicator is operational, the daytime running lamp on that side of the vehicleither reduces i intensity, t the side lamp level (all except NAS), or goes off (NAS).

The exterior lighting system is used for alarm arm and disarm requests to show alarm system status.

When the driver locks and arms the vehicle, a visual indication of a successful lock and arm request is displayed to the driver by asingle flash of the hazard warning lamps. the vehicle is superlocked, then the hazard wrning lamps wil flash a second time (200 ms off and 200 ms on) to confirm the superlock request.

If the alarm is activated, the hazard flashers are perated for 10, 30 second cycles of 200 ms on and 200 ms off with a 10 second delay between each cycle.

NOTE: n North American Specification NAS)vehicles, the delay betweenthe cycle when the alarm is activated is 60 seconds.

The chime is generated from the  sounder on receipt of a lights on signal, a driver door open signal and an igition off power mode 0 or accessory power mode 4 signal via a medium speed CAN bus signal from the CJB.

To operate the timer function the lighting control switch must be in one of the three headlamp timer positions when the ignition status is changed from ignition on power mode 6 to the off power mode .The timer function wil then be initiated and the low beam headlamps will be illuminated for the selected timer period.

The HLCM receives a power supply from the ignition relay in the E.The same power suppl is also supplied to the headlamp leveling motor i each headamp assembly. The front and rear height sensors are connected to the HLCM and receive a power and ground from the module. Each sensor has a signaline to the HLCM to return height information to the module. The module uses the height signals from the sensors to calculate the vehicle atitude and supplies a signal to each motor to power the headlamp to the required position.

Only the xenon headlamps use a filament bulb which is a D3S 35W. Allother lamps are iluminated by LED's and are non-servicable.  one LED in the lamp group fails, then allother LED's in that group are extinguished by the C.The affected lamp unit must be replaced.

The bi-xenon headamp uses a projector module which comprises an elipsoidal lens and a reflector. The projector reflector collets the light produced by the enon bul and project the light into a focal plane contining a shield.The contour of the shield is projected onto the road by the lens.

The headamps are not fitted with a tourist' lever. The headlamps require no adjustment for driving on the opposite drive hand as the beam pattern provides an optical solution.

WARnING: The Xenon system generates up to 30000 volts and contact with this voltage could lead to fatality. Make sure that the headlamps are switched off before working on the system.

The following safety precautions must be adhered to when working on the xenon low beam headlamp system:

DO NoT attempt any procedures on the xenon headlamps when the lights are switched on.   
Handling of the DS xenon bulb must be performed using suitable protective equipment; for example gloves and goggles. The glass part of the bulb must not be touched.   
Xenon bulbs must be disposed of as hazardous waste.   
Only operate the bulb in a mounted condition in the projector module installed in the headlamp.

The xenon headamp is known as 'bifunction' because it operates as both a low and high beam headamp unit. The xenon lamp, or High ntensity Discharge (HD amp as they are ometimesreferred to, comprises anellisoidal ens with a solenoid controlled shutter to change the beam output from low to high beam.

NOTE: If the lighting control switch i in the 'f position, the xenon lamp's high beam lamp will operate when the high eam 'flash' function is operated.

The xenon headamp system is controlled by the CB using a control module for each headamp and an igniter. The control modules and the igniters provide the regulated power supply required t illuminate the bulbs through their start-up phases of operation.

The xenon headamp is a selfcontained unit located within the headlamp assembly.The unit comprises a reflector, an adaptor ring, the lens, a shutter contrler and the xenon bulb, which together forms an asembly known as the projector module.The reflector is curved and provides the mounting point for the xenon bulb. The bulb locates in a keyway to ensure the correct alignment in the reflector and is secured by a plastic mounting ring. The bulb is an integral componnt of the igniter and is electrically connected by a connector located in the igniter unit.

The shutter controller is a solenoid which operates the shutter mechanism via a lever. The shutter is used to change the beam projection from low beam to high beam and vice versa.

The xenon bulbs illuminate when an arc of electrical current is established between 2 electrodes within the bulb.The xenon gas sealed in the bulb reacts to the electrical excitation and the heat generated by the current flow to produce the characteristic blue/white light.

To operate at fullefficency, the xenon bulb goes through  full tages of operation beforefulutput for continuousoperation is achieved. The 3 phases áare; start-up phase, warm-up phase and continuous phase.

In the start-up phase, the bul requires an initial high voltage starting pulse of up to 300 volts to estalish the ar. This is produced by the igniter. The warm-up phase begins once the arc is established. The xenon control module regulates the supply to the bulb to 2.6 which gives a lamp output of 75W.During this phase, the xenon gas begins to iluminate brightly and the environment within the bulb stabilizes, ensuring a continual current flow between the electrodes. When the warm-up phase is complete, the XBCM changes to continuous phase. The supply voltage to the bulb is reduced and the operating power required for continual operation is reduced to 35W. The process from start-up to continuous phase is completed in a very short time.

The XBCM (one per headlamp) receive an operating voltage from the C when the headamps are switched on. The modules regulate the power supply required through' the phases of start-up.

The igniters (one per hadamp) generate the initial high vltage required to establish the ar.The igniters have integral coils which generate high voltage pulses required for start-up. Once the xenon bulbs are operating, the igniters provide a closed circuit for the regulated power supply from the control modules.

The LED cornering lamps are an optional feature designed tilluminate the direction of travel when cornering at low speeds. The design of the lens projects a spread of light from the vehicle at approximately 45 degrees to the vehicle axis. The corering ampis incororatedinto the headamp assembly.The coering lamp L's are located in the headamp housing.

The cornering lamps are controlled by the left steering column multifunction switch with the lighting control switch in the headamp position or automatically when it is dark and the ignition in power mode7. The cornering lamps are supplied power via the ignition circuit to ensure that they do not function with the headamp delay feature. The cornering lamps are deactivated if the vehicle speed exceeds 25 mph (40 km/h). Only one cornering lamp willminate at any one time. If the left hand turn signal indicators are selected on, the left hand cornering lamp wil be iluminated and vice versa providing the vehicle speed and lighting control switch positions are correct.

Static Bending Lamps

The LED static bending lamps are designed to illuminate the direction of travel when cornering at low speeds. The static bending lamp functionality, which is controld by the and the HLCM, operates using iput from the steering angle sensor and vehicle speed information from the Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) module. The static bending lamp is incorporated into the headamp assembly. The design of the lens projects a spread of light from the vehicle at approximately 45 degrees to the vehicle axis. The static bending lamp uses a LED module which is connected via wires to the main connector on the headlamp housing.

The static bending lamps operate with a steering angle sensor CAN bus signal which i received by the C. The C monitors this signal and vehicle speed and activates the static bending lamp LED. When the operation parameters of the lamp are rached, the static bending lamps will snap on and fade ofWhen the lamp is witched of the  fades the LED off by decreasing the Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) voltage in a linear manner depending on steering angle and vehicle speed. The cornering lamps can only be active for a maximum of 3 minutes.

NOTE: Static bending lamps only operate when the transmission is in DRIVE or in SPORT.

The DRL are active when the engine is running and a gearis selected. When a turn signal indicator is active, the DRL intensit isreduced until the turn signal idicator is extinguished. When the side lamps are active, the DRL function i taken over by the functionality of the side lamps.

NOTES:

In certain markets the DRL are extinguished when the vehicle is stationary with the hand brake applied.

The automatic headamp function is a driver asstance system. The driver can override the system operation by selection of side lamp or headamp n if the ambient light conditions require front and rear lighting to be active. The automatic headamp system uses a light sensor and the , which are connected via a LI bus to control the headamp functionality. The light sensor is incorporated in the rain/ight sensor located on the inside of the windshield, below the rear view mirror. The wiper system also uses the rain/light sensor for automatic wiper operation.

Thelight sensor measures the ambient lght around the vehicle in a vertical diretion and also the angular light level from the front of the vehicle.The rainight sensor uses vehicle speedsignals, wiper switch position and the park position of the front wipers to control the system. The automatic headlamp operation uses ambient light levels which are monitored by a hotodieoporated inthe ghtensor.The ight esorsendlght onoffruest the   the s which responds by switching on the low beam headamps, front side lamps and rear tail lamps. The automatic headamps are activated under the following conditions:

Twilight   
Darkness   
Rain   
Snow   
Tunnels   
Underground or multistoried car parks.

Operation of the automatic headamps requires the ignition to be in ignition mode 6, the lighting control switch to be in the 'UTO' positio andlght o reuest sial rom the light sensor f the ainsenso ignal acivates the fat speed wipers, the low beam headlamps are activated, providing the lighting control switch is in the 'AUTO' position.

Some customers may complain of condensation/mist inside exterior lamps. Condensation/mist is a natural phenomenon which can occur when there is a temperature difference between the inside and outside of the lamp unit. This condensation is considered to be as a result of normal atmospheric conditions and replacing the light unit wil not correct this symptom. With theintroductio of clear lenses condensation i likel to be morenoticale but does not affect the performance of the lamp. Condensation wil clear when the lights have been on for some length of time and in warmer ambient temperatures

A lamp that exhibits condensation should be evaluated after a drying time where all the functions have been operated for a minimum of 30 minutes. If the condensation has started to clear during this time it indicates that the lamp seling has NOT been breached and will eventually clear. The lamp must NOT be replaced

CAUTION: Make sure that bulb covers are correctly installed and make sure that all breathers (tubes or membrane patches) are free from dirt and debris and are fitted correctly as these can allead to the formation of condensation. f any of these are determined to be the cause of the condensation, measures should be taken to dry out the lamps and to make sure that the bulb covers are installed correctly

The Owner's handbook clearly states that condensation may form on the inside of lamp lenses and is caused by atmospheric conditions. That it is not detrimental to lamp performance and willclear during normal usage

Pools of water and high levels of condensation would indicate that the lamps sealing has been compromised. Check for damage and inspect the condition of caps and breathers

Differing layout on the opposing sides of the vehicle can lead to different levels of condensation inside the lamps from side to side. As a result of this the rate at which condensation clears may also differ from side to side

Photographic evidence of the condensation levels prior to and after drying time should be provided with every returned part. Failure to do so may result in the claim being rejected

This information bulltin contains examples of normal condensation generated from atmospheric conditions. A thin mist can form on the interior of clear plasti lenses, this inot detrimental to the lamp's performance.This thin mist willeventually clear through normal use, exiting through the lamp's venting system

Condensation or moisture can be more noticeable during the months of spring and autumn when there is a likelihood of a higher moisturecontent in the ir. It can occur when there is a temperature iffrence on either side ofthe lens surface.This can often be see in the evening and morning sunshine or when cold water makes contact with a warm lamp lens. When a lamp is warmed unevenly by the sunshine the surface area in direct sunlight wil be approximately 10°C higher than the remainder of the lamp. When warm air circulates within the lamp and makes contact with the colder surfaces moisture can appear on the lens as water condenses out of the warmer air. Condensation may occur when washing a vehicle with cold water on a warm day or when the lamps are warm and vice versa. This is the same phenomena as with the formation of dew on the surface of a glass window pane

The regulator provides a controlled variable Direct Current (D) voltage output from the generator. wo electrical terminals are provided on the outer casing of the generator. ne terminal supplies the  (direct current voltage output from the generator to the batery positive terminl. The seond terminal provides the LIN bus conection betwen the regulator and the GWM.

The output from the generator is Alternating Current AC). A bridge rectifier within the generator converts the AC output to Direct Current (DC).

The generator comprises a rotor winding, which is rotated by the generator pulle via the acessory drive belt, a stator which is retained stationary within the generator housing, a voltage output regulator and bridge rectifier.

The rotor winding assembly rotates inside the stator winding. The rotor generates a magnetic field and the stator winding develops AC voltage and current flows from the induced magnetic field of the rotor.

The regulator monitors the battery and stator voltages. Depending on the measured voltages, the regulator wil adjust the amount of rotor field current to control generator output. The regulator is located within the generator housing.

The regulator will maintain a pre-determined charging system voltage level. If the charging system voltage falls below the predetrmined level the reulator wil increase the field current produced by the stator and the rotor, increasing the maetic fil which result in an inreased gerator output. f the chargig sstem voltae raisesave the predetermined vel the regulator will decrease field current , reducing the magetic field and decreasing the generator output.The regulator controls the field current by adjusting the power supplied to the rotor windings.

The following variants of generator are fitted to the specific engine types:

•V8 S/C 5.0L Petrol - Denso SC2 150A V6 3.0L S/C Petrol - Denso SC2 150A TDV6 3.0L Diesel - Denso SC6 220A GTDi 2.0L Petrol - Denso SC6 220A TD4 2.2L Diesel - Denso 180A

The primary task of the instrument cluster is to display current vehicle status through a series of analogue gauges, indicator lamps, and a LCD (liquid crystal display) message center. In addition to this, the instrument cluster:

Acts as a gateway between the medium speed and high speed CAN (controller area network) bus networks   
Isconnected by the L (loal ineronnect networkus to the stat control unit nd the steing wheeclocksprig   
Controls operation of the steering column adjust feature Refer to: Steering Column (211-04 Steering Column, Description and Operation).   
Acts as an interface for the passive anti-theft system. Refer to: Anti-Theft - Active (419-01A Anti-Theft - Active, Description and Operation).

Two analogue gauges are lcated in the instrument cluster: the speedometer and the tachometer. The speedometer is located on the LH lefthandsideof the instrument cluster.The tahometer i located on the RH righthandside of the istrument cluster and displays engine speeds up to 7000 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM) for the supercharged engine, 800 RPM for the naturally aspirated engines and 6000 RPM for diesel variants.

The message center is a LCD located in a central position in the cluster. The message center displays system status information including fuel quantity remaining.

### 16. Dynamic Stability Control (DSC) Warning / Operation Indicator


The turn signal indicators are controlled by the CJB on receipt of medium speed CAN bus signals from the instrument cluster.

The instrument cluster outputs a voltage to the turn signal indicator switch. The switch contains resistors of diffrent values. When the witch is operated in either the LH or RH direction, the voltage is passed to a ground connection in the instrument cluster which detects the reduced voltage supplied via the resistors. When the turn signal indicator switch is operated in the LH or RH direction, the instrument cluster detects the ground voltage and determines whether a LH or RH selection is made.

The instrument cluster transmits a medium speed CAN message to the CB for operation of the applicable turn signal indicators. The message can contain a number of states for each possile switch position and also an out of range low and high state for ciruit fault and an initial value for the switch neutral position. The turn signal indators are not ubject to the 3 second indicator check when the ignition is switched on.

The R software controls the flash rate of the warning indicator which sends 'ON' and 'OFF signals to the instrument cluster which flashes the indicators in a green color. During normal operation, the warning indicator flashes slowly, accompanied simultaneously by a sound from the instrument cluster sounder. f a fault exists, the RJ transmits a message to the instrument cluster which responds by displaying an appropriate message in the message center.

The hazard warning indicators are controlled by the  on receipt of a completed ground path from the hazard warning indicator switch. The CB outputs a medium speed CAN message to the instrument cluster which operates both the LH nd RH turn signal indicators simultaneously. The hazard warning indicators can operate with the ignition switched offand therefore, the CAN message from the CB will also carry a wake-up' message for the instrument cluster.

The Auto High Beam indicator (green) illuminates when auto high beam is enabled.

The MIL warning indicator i controlled by the EM and illuminated by the instrument cluster on receipt of a message on the high speed CAN bus from the ECM . The indicator is iluminated in an amber color for a 3-second indicator check when the ignition is switched on.

If the MIL remains iluminated after the engine is started or iluminates when driving, a fault is present and must be investigated at the earliest pportunity. Ilumination of the MIL warning indicator alerts the driver to an OD on-board diagnostic fault which willcause excessive emissions output.This may relate to either an engine management system fault or a transmission.

The green colored front fog lamp indicator iscontrolled by the C andiluminated by the instrument clusteron receipt of a front fog lamp on messae on the medium speed CAN bus rom the The idicator iilumiated for as long as thefront fog lamps are active.The front fog lamp indicator i not subject to the  second indicator check when the igition iswitched on.

The DSC warning lamp is controlled by the ABS module and illuminated by the instrument cluster in response to messages received on the high speed CAN bus. The indicator is iluminated in an amber color for the -second indicator check when the ignition is switched on. The DSC warning indicator is permanently iluminated in an amber color if the instrument cluster receives a high speed CAN message from the ABS module relating to one of the following faults:

Traction control fault   
Yaw control fault   
Engine drag torque control fault Panic Brake Assist (PBA) fault Signal missing relating to either traction control active, yaw control active or DSC switch input.

The above faults wil also generate an applicable DSC and ABS warning message in the message center. The DSC warning indicator wil flash at 2 Hz if the traction control or yaw control is active when the DSC system is enabled.

The ambience lighting system is controlled by the Central junction box (CJB).

Ambience lighting can be adjusted by the customer using selection available on the Touch Screen (TS). Selections on the TS are passed to the CJB via the medium speed Controller Area Network (CAN) comfort systems bus.

The CB controls the output voltage to the ambience lighting Light Emittig Diodes (LEDs) via a Pulse Width Modulation (PW) output. The PWM output allows the CJB to control the light intensity and the light combining effect.

The parking aid switch is located in the instrument panel switch pack, above the touch screen. The switch is the LH switch with an integral LED .

The switch is a non-latching push switch which allows the driver to select the parking aid system on or of. When pressed, the switch momentarily connects a ground to the parking aid module.

The LED indicates when the parking aid system is active. The LED is controlled by the parking aid module.

NOTE: The control switch allws the driver to activate/deactivate the parking aid system if operation is required or not required.

The anti-trap function is enabled for window closing in both the inching and one-shot modes. If the anti-trap feature is activated while a window is closing, the window motor is reversed for a preset period.

A Hallsensor, located in the window regulator motor, monitors the speed of the motor and if the speed decreases below a sel threshold, indicating an obstruction, the power feed to the motor is reversed so the window goes back down for preset time.

In an emergency the anti-trap function can be overridden by holding the window switch in the one-shot closed position.

After the battery has been disconnected iti necessary to initialize the door window motors to be able to operate the one-sho up function.

Where a sunlind module has been replaced, there is an initialization routine ailale on the dagnostic too.This requires a new module to be initiallyinstalled in the fully down position and running of the "Initialize Specified Function/Feature" diagnostic routine on the manufacturer approved diagnostic too. Alternatively, the sunblind may be initialized manually by following the procedures described below:

1.Raise the sunblind to top (fully retracted) position   
Press and hold the door window 'down' switch for 15 seconds (the sunblind wil go down and willthen be in   
initialization mode)   
Release door window drop switch and press door window 'down' switch again to drive blind full into lower block   
Activate window switch 'up' until the sunblind reaches the top (ful retracted) position and release switch   
5. The sunblind is now initialized and should have 'one-touch' functionality

The belt minder function provides warnings to the driver if the appropriate front safety belts are not fastened when driving. The belt minder function is controlled by the instrument cluster using:

High speed CAN (controller area network) bus messages, from the RCM (restraints control module) , to monitor the status of the front safety belts. An input from the occupant detection system to monitor the status of the front passenger seat (RoW. An input from the ccupant cassfication system to monito the status ofthe front pasenger seat ederalU.

When the inition i switched to on, the instrument clusteriluminates the safety belt warning indicator until one of the front safety belts is fastened or the belt minder function is triggered. The belt minder function is triggered when the ignition switc is in accessory/convenience and the following conditions coexist:

The belt minder function is enabled   
The vehicle is not in reverse   
Vehicle speed is initially set at 20 km/h (12mph) or more, then afterwards from 10 km/h (6mph) or more until ignition - cycled   
The driver safety belt or i the front passenger seat is occupied, the front passenger safety belt, is unfastened.

When the belt minder is triggered, the instrument cluster gnerates the follwing warnings for repeated 10 seonds for a tota of approximately 190 seconds.

NOTE: There are slight timing diferences between ROW and Federal USA (second is driver only, lights only) vehicles.

Flashes the safety belt warning indicator at 2 Hz

.fter 10 seconds the safety belt warning indicator changes from flashing to continuously iluminated for 20 seconds. While the igger conditions still coexist, the warnings are repeated every 30 seconds until one of the following occurs:

•Approximately 3 minutes has elapsed from when the warnings were first triggered   
The safety belt of each occupied front seat is fastened   
The ignition mode is position

For non-Federal USA vehicles the belt minder function can be enabled and disabled using the driver safety belt switch. The belt minder function can also be enabled and disabled using the recommended Jaguar diagnostic tool.

Successful completion of the change i indicated by a single chime and the safety belt warning indicator flashing five times, at 2 H.

Operation of the face level registers i cotrolled by the AT module, usingLIN bus messagest the integral stepper motors.   
The four registers operate together in both the opening and closing phases.

The face level reisters can be selected to run in one of two modes; 'utomatic' or 'always pen'. The mode is selected on the climate control screen of the TSD. Refer to: Navigation System (415-01 Information and Entertainment System, Description and Operation).

In the automatic mode, operation of the face level registers is synchronized with the engine START/STOP button. When the engine starts and the blower is on, the ATC module opens the registers. When the engine stops, the ATC module closes the registers.

If a face level register is fouled, when it receives an open or close request, the register concerned makes a number of attempts t reach the requested position. f thereistersill des not move, it ilt in the fouled position.The remining registers will continue to open and close as normal.

The automatic mode is disabled when the limate control system is off The ATC module closes the registers if they are open in the automatic mode and the climate control system is selected off.

Impact sensor

![](images/_MISSING_8829fe99978709ce41d04e6489e6a3fa3040490844e66daffc91e29f08f0c02a.jpg)

Impact sensors are installed in the front and both sides of the vehicle. The use of multiple impact sensors provides shorter air bag trigger times, through faster detection of lateral and longitudinal acceleration, and improves detection accuracy.

There are two front impact sensors, attached to the headlamp surround panel below the headlamps.

There are four side impact/pressure sensors located in the passenger compartment, as follows:

One attached to the base of each B/C pillar One attached to the base of each D pillar.

Each impact sensor incorporates an accelerometer and a microchip powered by a feed from the RCM. The power feed also provides the interface connection through which the side impact sensor communicates with the RCM using serial data messages. Accleration is evaluated by the microchip and transmitted to the RCM, which then makes the decision on whether or not to activate the air bags and pretensioners.

When the ignition is switched on the RCM suppies power to the impact sensors, which perform a selftest. After satisfactory self tests the impact sensors continually output 'igital acleration' messagesto theRM. f a fault is detected therelevant impact sensor sends a fault message, istead of the digital aceleration message, to the RCM. The RCM then stores a related fault code and illuminates the air bag warning indicator. Fault can be retrieved by the Jaguar approved diagnostic system from the RCM via the high speed CAN bus connection.

A safety belt switch i installed in the buckle of each front safety belt to provide the RM with a status signal of the related safety belt(s). When the safety belt is unfastened the switch outputs a low current to the RCM. When the safety belt is fastened the switch outputs a high current to the RCM.

The exterior mirrors incorporate the following:

Blind spot monitoring indicator Auto dimming function Turn signal indicators Approach lamps Exterior temperature sensor Heated mirror function Reverse dipping function

Movement of the door mirrors is controlled from a switch pack located on the drivers door. The switch pack contains 2 non-latching mirror select buttons labeled 'L' and 'R'and à 4-way mirr movement switch. Door mirror movement commands are transmitted to the driver's door module over the Li (local iterconnect network) bus.The drivers door module transmits any mirror movement commands to the passenger door module over the medium speed CAN (controller area network) bus.

Movement of the door mirrors is carried out by the respective door module. The door modules provide supply and ground paths to the mirror motors and monitor mirror position via potentiometers located in the mirror housings.

Both exterior door mirros and the interior mirro feature an auto dimming function. The interio rear view mirro contains one forward and one reward facinglight sensor.The light sensors control the uto dimming feature of the interior mirro to reduce glare from the headlights of following vehicles.

When auto-dimming of the interior mirror is required, a supply is provided by the interior mirror to both door mirrors to initiate the door mirror auto-dimming sequence.

Blind spot monitoring function alerts the driver to a vehicle lcated i the vehicle blind spot.A warning indicatori lcated in each exterior mirror towards the outer edge. Refer to: Blindspot Monitoring System (413-09 Warning Devices, Description and Operation).
