### Front Belt Minder Function


The belt minder function provides warnings to the driver if the appropriate front safety belts are not fastened when driving. The belt minder function is controlled by the instrument cluster using:

High speed CAN (controller area network) bus messages, from the RCM (restraints control module) , to monitor the status of the front safety belts. An input from the occupant detection system to monitor the status of the front passenger seat (ROW). An input from the occupant classfiation system to monitor the status of the front passenger seat (Federal USA).

hen the ignition is switched to on, the instrument cluster illuminates the safety belt warning indicator until one of the front fety belt i fastened or the belt minder function i triggered. The belt minder function is triggered when the igition switch in áccessory/convenience and the following conditions coexist:

•The belt minder function is enabled   
The vehicle is not in reverse   
ehicle speed i initially set at 20 km/h (12mph) or more, then afterwards from 10 km/h (6mph) or more until ignition - cycled   
The driver safety belt or, if the front passenger seat is occupied, the front passenger safety belt is unfastened.

When the belt minder is triggered, the instrument cluster generates the follwing warnings for repeated 10 seconds for a tota of approximately 190 seconds.

NOTE: There are slight timing diffrences between ROW and Federal USA (second is driver only, lights only) vehicles.

Flashes the safety belt warning indicator at 2 Hz

After 10 seconds the safety belt warning indicator changes from flashing to continuously iluminated for 20 seconds. While the rigger conditions still coexist, the warnings are repeated every 30 seconds until one of the following occurs:

Approximately 3 minutes has elapsed from when the warnings were first triggered   
•The safety belt of each occupied front seat is fastened   
The ignition mode is position 0

For non-Federal USA vehicles the belt minder function can be enabled and disabled using the driver safety belt switch. The belt minder function can also be enabled and disabled using the recommended Jaguar diagnostic tool.

Successful completion of the change i indicated by a single chime and the afety belt warning indicator flashing five times, a 2 Hz.

Safety Belt Warning Indicator

![](images/_MISSING_76f31c2039e74d8e9615278ac4d2258d151cca6e5102b760711a9fd39f5aa12b.jpg)

E139622

In addition, an audible warning willsound under the following conditions:

The seat belt of an occupied front seat is not fastened or is unfastened during a journey A rear seat belt is unfastened.

NOTE: If a heavy object is placed on the front passenger seat, it may activate the Beltminder feature. It is recommended that any objects placed on the front passenger seat are secured using the seat belt.

The RCM is installed on the top of the transmission tunnel, in line with the B pilars, and controls operation of the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS). The main functions of the RCM include:

Crash detection and recording   
Air bag and pre-tensioner firing   
Selftest and system monitoring, with status indication via the air bag warning lamp and non-volatile storage of fault information.o.

The RCM determines which elements of the SRS are to be deployed by using two internal areas:

•Crash severity evaluation Deployment handler.

Crash severity evaluation evaluates crash severity by using data from the RCM internal accelerometer, the front crash sensor and the safety belt buckle sensor. Based on this data, the RCM decides which level of air bag module deployment is required and forwards the information to the second area, the deployment handler.

The deployment hander evaluates the status of the seat track position sensor and safety belt buckle sensors before a decision is made about which restraints should finally be deployed.

Data from the side crash sensors is used by the RCM in conjunction with acceleration data from the RCM internal accelerometer to make a deployment decision. The RCM processes the accleration data and subject to an impact being of high enough severity, decides whether the side air bag module should be deployed.

On board testing of the air bag modules, front safety belt pretensioner firing circuits, warning indicator circuits and module status (the crash and side impact sensors perform basic selftest is performed by the RCM together with the storing offault codes.

The RCM drives the SRS indicator on the instrument pack via a CAN signal. f the warning lamp fail, a fault code is recorded and a warning tone is sounded in place of the lamp if a further fault occurs. It also provides a temporary back-up power suply to operate the air bag modulesi theevent that i crash conitions, the battey suppy i ost. n theevent of a crash, it records certain data which can be accessed via the diagnostic connector.

A saving sensor in the RCM provides cofirmation of an impact to verify if air bag and pretensioner activation is necessary. Various firing strategies are employed by the RCM to ensure that during an accident only the appropriate air bags and pretensioners are fired. The firing strategy used also depends on the inputs from the safety belt switches and the occupant monitoring system.

An energy reserve in the RCM ensures there is always a minimum of 150 miliseconds of stored energy available if the powe supply from the igition switch is disrupted during a crash. The stored energy is sufiient to produce firing signals for the driver air bag, the passenger air bag and the safety belt pretensioners.

When the ignition is switched on the RM performs a selftest and then perfrms cyclical monitoring of the system. f a fault isdetected the RM stores a related fault code andiluminates the air bag warning indicator. The faults can be retrieved by the recommended Jaguar dianostic tol ver the AN bus. If a fault that could cuse a false fire signal is detected, the RCM disables the respective firing circuit, and keeps it disabled during a crash event.

The driver air bag module is controlled by the RCM which chooses between single or dual stage deployment, depending on the occupant position and the crash severity.To reduce therisk of anair bag module induced injury to a driverthat is positioned close to the stering wheel, the air bag module deploys radially. It has a non-side propllnt that reduces particulates and fluents. It consist of a two stage iflator with separate chambers for the two ifation stages, each being independently activated by the RCM. It has two electrical connectors that are color coded and mechanically keyed to the respective connector on the inflator.

Impact sensor

![](images/_MISSING_240d0a439d16e41a86333792db5f50d5a1d94df46259a8850d64ac4b5c72aaee.jpg)

Impact sensors are installed in the front and both sides of the vehicle. The use of multiple impact sensors provides shorter air bag trigger times, through faster detection of lateral and longitudinal acceleration, and improves detection accuracy.

There are two front impact sensors, attached to the headlamp surround panel below the headlamps.

There are four side impact/pressure sensors located in the passenger compartment, as follows:

One attached to the base of each B/C pillar One attached to the base of each D' pillar.

Each impact sensor incorporates an accelerometer and a microchip powered by a feed from the RCM. The power feed also provides the interface connection through which the side impact sensor communicates with the RCM using serial data messages. Accleration is evaluated by the microchip and transmitted to the RCM, which then makes the decision on whether or not to activate the air bags and pretensioners.

When the ignition is switched on the RCM suppies power to the impact sensors, which perform a selftest. After satisfactory self tests the impact sensors continually output 'igital acleration' messagesto theRM. f a fault is detected therelevant impact sensor sends a fault message, istead of the digital aceleration message, to the RCM. The RCM then stores a related fault code and illuminates the air bag warning indicator. Fault can be retrieved by the Jaguar approved diagnostic system from the RCM via the high speed CAN bus connection.

System Operation   
![](images/_MISSING_9af834ac3cc2fe92fb249f0465f359786d604867c5f703196f78ee2fd777ea8e.jpg)

Operation of the wipers and washers i controlled by the  central junction box) i response to driver iputs from the wiper control switch and signals from the rain/ight sensor. The I monitors the condition of the wiper/washer control switch and transmits driver requests to the CJB over the medium speed CAN bus.

The wiper control switch is connected via hardwired connections to the . The I outputs on 4 wires a reference voltage to the wash/wipe switch, the auto wiper switch, the wiper switch and the flick wipe switch.Al the witches are connected to the IC on a common ground. Each switch function is connected to ground via a resistor or series of resistors and the  monitors the ground signal and determines which function has been selected. The I then outputs the appropriate message on the medium speed CAN bus to the C which responds to the requested wiper function. The CB then activates the appropriate function either directly or via relays in the EJB (engine junction box) for the wipers and headlamp washers.

NOTE: Rear window washer uses the same washer reservoir and washer pump as the windshield washer.

The windshield and rear window washers are controlled by the  . A driver request for washer operation, via the wiper control switch, is passed to the  on the LIN bus. The I passes the message to the CB on the medium speed CAN bus.

The C energizes the windshield washer pump during the up stroke of the first 2 wash/wipe cycles. This ensures that wiper fluid is pushed to the sides of the windshild and eliminates the trail of fluid which can occurif the fluid is pushed to the bottom of the windshieldThe wipers wil continue for more cycles, follwedafter a delay of4 seonds, by asingle dry wipe.

NOTE: The dry wipe feature is configurable using an approved Jaguar diagnostic system.

The operation of the washer pump on the wiper up stroke only is configurable using an approved Jaguar diagnostic system.

The washer button can be pressed and held and the wipers willoperate continuously for up to 10 seconds. After this period when the button i released, the wipers wil continue for  more cycles, fllwed after a delay, by asingle dry wipe.After this period washing will be iibited, the wipers wil continue for 3 more cyles, follwed after a delay, by a single dry wipe. Reactivating the switch will recommence the wash/wipe cycle.

The headamp washer is activated when the driver requests windshield washer operation. The  receives the driver request via a CAN bus message from the C.The  then checks for an exterio lights active signal and that a low washer fluid level signal is not present.

The  outputs a control vltage to a headamp washer pump relay located in the The relay ienergied by thefor a pre-determined period to allow the headlamp telescopic washers to operate.

The CB monitors the driver washer request and only operates the headamp washer on every fourth request for windshield washer operation, provided that 10 minutes have elapsed since the last headamp washer operation. The washer sequence is reset when the headlamps or the ignition is switched off.

NOTE: If a low fluid reservoir level is present, the CJB prohibits headlamp powerwash.

### WARNING: The following precautions MUST be adhered to when working on the SRS sy


See also Fire.

Used in sound and noise insulation. Cured foams used in seat and trim cushioning.

Follow manufacturer's instructions.

Unreacted components are irritating and may be harmful to the skin and eyes. Wear gloves and goggles.

Individuals with chronic respiratory diseases, asthma, bronchial medical problems, or histories of llergic diseases should not work in or near uncured materials.

The components, vapors or spray mists can cause direct irrtation, sensitivity reactions and may be toxic or harmful.

Vapors and spray mists must not be inhaled. These materials must be applied with adequate ventilation and respiratory protection. Do not remove the respirator immediately after spraying, wait until the vapor/mists have cleared.

Burning of the uncured components and the cured foams can generate toxic and harmful fumes. Smoking, naked flames or the use of electrical equipment during foaming operations and until vapors/mists have cleared should not be allwed. Any heat cutting of cured foams or partially cured foams should be conducted with extraction ventilation.

All vehicles with the passenger air bag installed from the factory have a warning sticker attached to the instrument panel, prohibiting the use of rear facing child seats in the front seating position. Failure to follw this instruction may result in personal injury.

The SRS contains components which are potentially hazardous to service personnel i not handed correctly.The following guidelines and precautions are intended to alert personnel to potential sources of danger and emphasise the importance of ensuring the integrity of the SRS components installed to the vehicle.

The correct procedures must always be used when working on SRS components. Persons working on the SRS system must be fully trained and have been issued with the safety guidelines.   
The airbag modules contain extremely flammable and hazardous compounds. Contact with water, acids or heavy metals may produce harmful or explosive results. Do not dismantle, incinerate or bring into contact with electricity before the unit has been deployed. Always replace a seat belt assembly that has withstood the strain of a severe vehicle impact or if the webbing shows signs of fraying. Always disconnect the vehicle battery before carrying out any electric welding on a vehicle installed with an SRS system.

CAUTION: Do not expose airbag modules or seat belt pre-tensioners to temperatures exceeding 85° C (185° F.

It should be noted that these precautions are not restricted to operations performed when servicing the SRS system. The same care should be exercised when working on ancillay systems and components located in the vicinity of SRS components; these include but are not limited to:

Steering wheel airbag, rotary coupler.   
Passenger front airbag.   
Head airbag modules - front and rear.   
Seat belt pre-tensioners.   
SRS harnesses, link leads and connectors.   
Side (thorax) air bags.

Take care not to trap airbag modules when installing interior trim components.

Make sure SRS components are not contaminated by oil or grease.

NOTES:

Following seat belt pre-tensioner deployment, the seat belts can stil be used as conventional seat belts but will need to be replaced as soon as possible to make sure full SRS protection.

If the SRS components are to be replaced, the part number/bar code of the new unit must be recorded.

Never drop an SRS component. The airbag diagnostic control unit is a particularly shock sensitive device and must be handled with extreme care. Airbag modules and seat belt pre-tensioners could deploy if subjected to a strong shock. Never wrap your arms around an airbag module. If a module has to be carried, hold it by the cover with the cover uppermost and the base away from your body.   
Never transport airbag modules or seat belt pre-tensioners in the passenger compartment of a vehicle. Always use the luggage compartment of the vehicle for carrying airbag modules and seat belt pre-tensioner units.   
Never attach anything to an airbag cover or any trim component covering an airbag module. Do not allow anything to rest on top of an airbag module.   
Always keep components cool, dry and free from contamination.   
Never apply grease or cleaning solvents to seat belt pre-tensioner units, component failure could result.   
Always store an airbag module with the deployment side uppermost. If it is stored deployment side down, accidental deployment will propel the airbag module with sufficient force to cause serious injury.   
Keep new airbag modules in their original packaging until just prior to installing.Place the old module in the empty packaging for carriage.

![](images/_MISSING_2ad17911a85eb0e63fa966ac796520cc8cebda36d2d7d993a80d5fec61212263.jpg)

WARNINGS:

When handing an iflatable tubular structure ITS) airbag module, hold by the gas generator housing, Do NoT hold by the airbag. Do not wrap the thumb around the gas generator while holding. Do not drape irbag over shoulder or around neck. For seat buckle type pre-tensioners, hold by the piston tube, with the open end of the piston tube pointing towards the ground and the buckle facing away from your body. Do not cover the end of the piston tube. Do NoT hold buckle type pre-tensioners by the bracket assembly or cable. Never point the piston tube towards your body or other people.

Airbag modules and seat belt pre-tensioners are classed as explosive devices. For overnight and longer term storage, they must be stored in a secure steel cabinet which has been approved as suitable for the purpose and has been registered with the local authority.

Store airbag modules or seat belt pre-tensioners in a designated storage area. If there is no designated storage area available, store in the locked luggage compartment of the vehicle and inform the workshop supervisor.

WARNINg: During deployment parts of the airbag module become hot enough to burn you. Wait 30 minutes after deployment before touching the airbag module.

Deployment procedures and precautions as detailed in this manual should be strictly adhered to. Only personnel who have undergone the appropriate training should undertake deployment of airbag and pre-tensioner modules. The following precautions must be complied with:

Only use deployment equipment approved for the intended purpose. Deployment of airbag / pre-tensioner modules must be performed in a well ventilaed area which has been designated for the purpose. Make sure airbag / pre-tensioner modules are not damaged or ruptured before attempting to deploy. Where local legislation exists, notify the relevant authorities of intention to deploy airbag and pretensioner units. When deploying airbag pre-tensioner units, make sure that al personnel are at least 15 metres (45 feet) away from the deployment zone. Make sure deployment tool is connected correctly, in compliance with the instructions detailed in the SRS section of this manual. In particular, make sure deployment too is NOt connected to battery supply before connecting to airbag module connector. When deploying seat belt pre-tensioners, make sure pre-tensioner unit is secured correctly to the seat. When removing deployed airbag modules and pre-tensioner units, wear protective clothing. Use gloves and seal deployed units in a plastic bag. Following deployment of any component of the SRS system within the vehicle, al SRS components must be replaced. DO NOT reuse or salvage any parts of the SRS system. Do not lean over an airbag module when connecting deployment equipment.

If a vehicle i to be scrapped, undeployed airbag modules and pre-tensioner units must be manull deployed. In this case irbags can be deployed in the vehicle. Before deployment, make sure the irbag module is secure within its correct mounting position.Deployment of the driver's arbag in the veicle may damage thesteering wheel; ithe vehicle not being srapped, deploy the module outside of the vehicle.

The Restraints Control Module (RCM) wilog a crash fault after every impact which is severe enough to cause airbag deployment. It is possile to have threecrashesimpact logged after one vent where, for example, afront, sideand rollover has occurred. After the third fault is logged, the SRS warning lamp will b illuminated and the RM must be installed. After any airbag deployment a new RCM must be installed.

The SRS side impact sensor must be replaced if there are any signs of physical damage or if the restraints control module (RCM) is registering a fault.

The following information details the policy for replacement of SRS components as a result of a vehicle accident.

Impacts which do not deploy the airbags or pre-tensioners

Check for structural damage in the area of the impact paying particular attention to bumper armatures, longitudinals and bracketry.

The replacement and inspection policy is dependent on the type and severity of the crash condition. The following guidelines are the minimum that should be exercised as a result of the deployment of specific SRS components.

Check for structural damage in the area of impact paying particular atention to bumper armatures, longitudinals and bracketry.

Driver airbag module

Rear seat belt pre-tensioners - if installed   
Driver's seat belt retractor - if installed   
Rotary coupler

Restraints control module (RCM) if the three crashes/impacts have been stored

Rear seat belt buckles, webbing, buckle covers, body anchorage points and tongue latching function   
Fascia moulding adjacent to passenger airbag module   
Steering wheel   
Front seat frames and head restraints   
Steering column - if adjustment is lost or if there are signs of collapse   
Seat belt height adjusters   
Rear seat belts

Side Air Bags

Side (thorax) airbag Any side impact sensors that have been physically damaged or if a fault is being registered Restraints Control Module (RCM) if the three crashes/impacts have been stored

Door trim casing

Rear seat belts

Head airbag modules

Airbag retaining clips   
Internal trim finisher   
Front seat belt buckle pre-tensioners

Restraints Control Module (RCM) if the three crashes/impacts have been stored

Additionally, the following items must be inspected for damage and replaced as necessary:

Headlining   
Component mounting brackets   
Front seat belts, retractors and webbing, tongue latching function, 'D' loop and body anchorage points   
Rear seat belt buckles, webbing, buckle covers, tongue latching function, and body anchorage points   
•Adjacent trim components   
Seat belt height adjusters

Rear impacts

cAUtioN: If the seat belt pre-tensioners are deployed during a rear impact, the follwing components must be eplaced:

Seat belt pre-tensioners   
Front and rear seat belt retractors used during the impact   
Restraints Control Module (RCM) if the three crashes/impacts have been stored

The intrusion detection module comprises an ultrasonic sound wave sensor which monitors the vehicle's interior.

The intrusion detection module is activated with volumetric mode which in turn is enabled when the vehicle is double locked. The vehicle can be locked and alarmed with the module de-activated i a pet is to be left in the vehicle for example by single-locking the active antitheft system. The intrusion detection modules can also be de-ctivated by deselecting the 'Alarm Sensors oton in theehicle Setngs screen on the Touch Screen Display.

NoTE: The Touch Screen method of de-activation of the intrusion detection module is only for one arm cycle, it will 'evert to active once the engine is next started.

The registerscontrol the flow and direction of ir from the ir duct. The instrument panel cotains four fae level reisters; one at each end and two mounted central. For the rear seat occupants, two registers are installed in the rear face of the center floor console. Allof the registers incorporate vertical and horizontal directional vane adjustment and fulair flow adjustment down to zero.

The four face level reisters in the instrument panel each contain an integral stepper motor. The stepper motors enable the registers to rotate between the open and closed positions. In the open position, the registers have normal appearance and functionality. In the closed position, the registers present a smooth surface flush with the surrounding instrument panel.

The vents are fixed outlet. There are four vents in the upper surface of the instrument panel; one in each end to direct air onto the side windows and two along the front edge to direct air onto the windshield.

The battery saver provides an automatic shut-offof the interior lamps after a period of 15 minutes in order to prevent excessive power drain on the battery.

When the ignition mode is changed from the ignition power mode 6 or accssory power mode 4 to the of power mode 0, the CB starts a timer which de-energizes a delayed power of relay in the , removing the power supply to the interior lamps after a period of 15 minutes, switching off al or any interior lamps which have remained on for any reason.

Once the timer has expiredand the lamps are off any one of the follwing will wake up' the battery saver and the interior lamps wil function agin. The tmer wil be restarted assoon as an input is reeived by the  from one of the follwing:

Ignition mode changed from of power mode 0 to accessory power mode 4, ignition power mode 6 or crank power mode 9.   
Any door, including the luggage compartment lid is opened   
An unlock request is received from the Smart Key via the KVM   
Front overhead console interior lamp is switched on via the JaguarSense function.

When the interior lighting system switches the interior lamps on the  ramps the lamps up to fullpower over a period of 1.3 seconds. When the system switches the lamps off after the time-ut period hasexpired, the fades the lamps offover a period of 2.6 seconds.

The interior lighting system willilluminate the interior lamps when one of the following events occurs:

The CJB receives an unlock signal from the Smart Key via the KVM   
Any door is opened including the luggage compartment lid   
The ignition mode is changed from ignition power mode 7 to power mode 4.   
The interior lights will o on when the vehicle oesfrom power mode7 to 4 or when a door is opened or when the vehicle is unlocked or when they are manually requested.

The interior lighting system will turn off the interior lamps when one of the following events occurs:

Once the time-out timer delay has expired since the lamps were either activated or the last door is closed and the vehicle is not locked   
The ignition i in of power mode  and an external lock is requested using either the door lock buttons or the Smart Key) with all doors closed   
The interior light wil o of when the vehicle is locked (power mode  or the timeout reaches  or when they are manually turned off.

### Navigation System - Navigation System Antenna Removal and Installation


The CB is an integrated unit located on the right 'A' pillr, below the instrument panel.The  cotains fuses, relays and number of microprocessors which control the power suppy and functionality of the interior lighting system and other vehicle systems.

The RB is located on the right side of the luggage compartment. The R contains fuses, relays and microprocessors which in conjunction with the CJB control the interior lighting system and other vehicle systems.

The C and the R provide circuit protection for allinterior lamp circuits. The lamps are protected by fuses i the CJ and the RJB.

The footwellamps are located under the instrument panel. Each lamp comprises a bulb and holder which is part of the instrument panel wirig harness.The bulb and holder is located ina hole in the front footwelair ducts.The footwellamps are active at all times when the interior lamps are active.

- Diagnosis: - Ingress of water into side luggage compartment area

Cause:

The forced air extraction for the vehicle interior is located in the quarter panel lower extension.   
The rubber flap of the forced air extraction must be able to move freely.

Corrective action:

-Remove the forced air extraction.   
Check the seal area between the bodywork and housing, as well as the rubber flap.   
-Renew seal if necessary.

DSB (Dynamic Seat Belts is an option fited from 12MY. This has an electric motor which pretensions the belt prior to a crash and is triggered by the CMbB (Crash Mitigation by Braking) system.

In addition, an audible warning will sound under the following conditions:

The seat belt of an occupied front seat is not fastened or is unfastened during a journey A rear seat belt is unfastened.

NOTE: If a heavy object is placed on the front passenger seat, it may activate the Beltminder feature. It is recommended that any objects placed on the front passenger seat are secured using the seat belt.

### Passenger Airbag Deactivation Switch (All Except NAS)


The registerscontrol theflow andirectionofir from the ir duct.The instrument panel cotains four fae leel reisters; one at each end and two mounted centrally. For the rear seat occupants, two registers are installed in the rear face of the center floor console. Allof the registers incorporate vertical and horizontal directional vane adjustment and fullair flow adjustment down to zero.

The four fae level registers in the instrument panel each contain an integral stepper motor. The stepper motors enable the registers to rotate between the open and closed positions. In the open position, the registers have normal appearance and functionality. In the closed position, the registers present a smooth surface flush with the surrounding instrument panel.

The vents are fixed outlet. There are four vents in the upper surface of the instrument panel; one in each end to direct air onto the side windows and two along the front edge to direct air onto the windshield.

Central Face Level Registers

![](images/_MISSING_b7aa0f7bc0350b37010691c2448d46710837200243dad4e9f6228bbfcaeb3615.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_b85dd517e744635e472c6fb00bca7316a495e7bea96ab9b86f75d61fdf50f0b5.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_ea06dcc71b7dcdc76a19daed96b252168f74ee4fcb57a0c012f8c33ab361f2b9.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_fe1f4fc5cfeaf8a008d9843dce2782e6c37cbbf7cbfa3402133f6e0ccadb41a2.jpg)

The Passenger airbag is controlled by the RCM which chooses between single or dual stage deployment, depending on the occupant status and the crash severity. It consists of a two stage inflator with two air bag electrical connectors to accommodate the two stage inflation.

The heated gas iflator consists of a high-pressure mix of clean air and hydrogen gas, triggered by two separate ignition squibs. It produces a controlled generation of clean gasto rapidy fil the air bag.It i classied as a stored flammable gas (not as an explosive) and as such, has less restrictive storage and transportation requirements. It produces a very clean burr and almost no particulates and is almost free of any toxins, making disposal or recycling much easier.

Side air curtain

![](images/_MISSING_a17f2cade4b64b5d950993f2e931eaa223f1e6756c381f0f16440c35d4383607.jpg)

E144786

Side air curtains protect against head injuries in a side impact.

A single iflator mounted behind the rear seat unfurls the curtain and fil five separate chambers to provide head protection cushions for occupants in side-impact and roll-over events. Steel ramps guaranteethe curtain does not snag on the interior trim as it unfurls, while tethers at the front and rear of the curtain ensure the curtain is held taut.

![](images/_MISSING_67ff05cab109a0dbb5d54775f01452f88fd8c9b7038f366e3ed8dcc9a7a4a67c.jpg)

E144787

A side air bag is attached to the outside of each front seat backrest frame, under the backrest cover.

The side air bags are handed and each consist of a fabric cover which contains the folded air bag and the infator. The seat harness conects the igniter of the inflator to a connector in the main seat harness conector block located under the front edge of the seat cushion.

When the air bag deploys it opens the fabric cover and splits open the backrest seat cover at the front sear

The side air bags use a solid propellant medium. The inflated volume of each side air bag is 20 liters.

The seat position sensor allows the RM to detect when the driver seat is forward of a given point on the seat track. The seat position sensor consists of a Haleffet sensoratached to the driver seat frame. While the iition i on, the RM supplies the sensor with power, and monitors the return current. When the seat frame moves forwards, the sensor moves over the edge of the seat track, which changes the reluctance of the sensor. The change of current is detected by the RCM and used as a switching point. The switching point is when the center of the sensor is  4 mm from the leading edge of the seat track.

When the driver seat is forward of the witching point, the RM increases the time delay between firing the two stages of the inflator in the driver air bag. When the driver seat is rearward of the switching point, the RCM uses the normal time delay between firing the two stages.

![](images/_MISSING_36a59df2b1bc229b320a626aa6a5fab346a7d5a59c47a03f3191d4e0dc6f3928.jpg)

The air bag warning indicator consists of a red Light Emitting Diode (LED) behind a SRS graphic in the instrument cluster.

Operation of the air bag warning indicator is controlled by a high speed CAN bus message from the RCM to the instrument cluster. The RCM sends the signal to illminate the air bag warning indicator if a fault is detected, and for approximately 6 seconds during the bulb check at the beginning of each ignition cycle.

Passenger Airbag Deactivation Warning Lamp

![](images/_MISSING_e3a7a0ae59461868aab5888ebabe906263bc7f6b97230e8881fd27866b883a1e.jpg)

The passenger air bag deactivatio indicator i installed on the center switch pack of the instrument panel. When appropriate, the indicato illuminates to advise front seat occupants that the passenger air bag i disabled. Operation of the indicator is controlled by the RCM. The RCM illuminates the indicator when:

There is a fault with the passenger air bag firing circuit(s).   
The passenger air bag is deactivated with the passenger air bag deactivation switch (where fitted).   
Required by passenger seat occupant monitoring (see below).

The passenger air bag deactivation switch provides a method of manually disabling the passenger air bag. The switch is installed in the front passenger end of the instrument panel and operated by the ignition key.

When the passenger air bag deactivation switch is operated, it changes a ground connection between two pins in the connectors of the RCM. When the passenger ir bag deactivation switch i selected to F the RCM disables the passengerir bag and, if the front passenger seat is occupied, illuminates the passenger air bag deactivation indicator.

### Occupant Classification System


![](images/_MISSING_f02bef6606a3727348ef96295f70bca3008fe286dac0c03f0fe8d6a1b2e4afe3.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_60d8d39e1466c96c2f5f778c3a652a7602f2cadbe18a5011e4b8816a29a4d0a2.jpg)
The occupant classification system can determine if the front passenger seat is unoccupied, occupied by a small person, or occupied by a large person. The occupant classification system consists of:

A pressure pad, installed under the cushion of the front passenger seat, which is connected to a pressure sens A safety belt tension sensor, integrated into the anchor point of the front passenger safety belt An occupant classification module, installed under the front passenger seat.

he pressure pad is a silicone filled bladder. Any load on the pressure pad is detected by the pressure sensor.

The safety belt tension sensor is a strain gauge that measures the load applied by the safety belt anchor to the anchor bolt.   
The sensor is located in the lower safety belt anchor point.

The emergency locking etractor incorporates two mechanical inertia devices. One inertia device activates if the safety belt is subjected to a sharp pull The second inertia device activates if the vehicle is subject to a sudden deceleration or i on a severe incline.

North American Speification (NAS) safety belt retractors also include an automatic locking feature. The Automatic Locking Retractor ALRis fited to allpassengerseating positions andallws the sfety belt to betesioned to aid the safitment f child or booster seats. For additional information, refer to the Owners Handbook.

NAS vehicles are also fitted with a belt tension sensor on the front passenger seat. The belt tension sensori incorporated int the seat belt lower anchorage and is attached to the seat frame by an M Torx head bolt. The belt tension sensor forms part of the SRS (supplemental restraint system) occupancy detection and classification feature.

The center rear safety belt features a mini-buckle lower anchorage.The mini-buckle idisengaged by iserting a suitable tool into the small aerture on the front face of the housing.

The TS receives  fused power suppy from the RB (rear junction box) After selecting the seat heating/limate seat menu on Integrated Control Panel P), one of the three seat heat temperature seletions made by the driver or passenger using the TS soft keys are passed from the TS on the medium speed CAN bus to the ICP. The ICP processes the information and transmits the request on the medium speed CAN bus to the ATC (automatic temperature control) module.

The seat cushion heater element has a thermal sensor which supplies a fedback signal back to the CB (entral junction box) The backrest heater elements do not have a thermal sensor and are maintained at the same temperature as the seat cushion elements.

The ATC module reacts to the driver request information received from the CP and requests the CB to activate the seat heaters. The CB measures the returned temperature signals from the thermal sensors and relays the temperature signals back to the ATC module. The ATC module then uses the measured seat element temperatures to provide closed-loop control of the heater elements to maintain the temperature at one of the three heat ranges selected.

NOTE: To prevent excessive battery discharge, the heated front seats willonly operate when the engine is running.

The TS receives a fused power suppy from the RJ.After selecting the seat heating/limate seat menu, selections made by the driver using the TS soft keys are passed from the TS on the mdium speed CAN bus to the P. The ICP processes the information and transmits the request on the medium speed CAN bus to the SCCM.

The SCCM receives its power supplies from the . Heating and cooling requests are generated using the soft keys on the TS. These requests are transmitted to the P over the medium speed CAN bus. The P forwards these requests to the SCCM over the medium speed CAN bus.

The SCCM supplies power to the two climate modules in each seat. The temperature sensor in each limate module is monitored by the SCM which uses the temperature information to control the Peltier cell accordingly and also the cooling fan motors to distribute the heated or cooled air.

NOTE: To prevent excessive battery discharge, the heated and cooled front seats wil only operate when the engine is running.

The CB supplies 3 power supplies to the driver seat switchpack. The fused supplies provide power for the seat height and backrest recline, the seat forward/rearward and seat tit and the lumbar adjustment respectively. The  only provides the power to the driver seat switchpack when the ignition is on (power mode 6).

For the seat movement motors, when the applicable switch is operated, the power is suppled to the applicable side of the motor and the ground path is completed to operate the motor in the required direction.To move the motor in the opposite direction the polarity is reversed.

For the lumbar adjustment, when the switch is operated in the inflate position, power is supplied to the pump motor to inflate the lumbar support. When the switch is operated in the opposite direction, the power energizes a solenoid which in tur open a valve to deflate the lumbar support.

### Electric Driver Seat Adjustment - Memory Seats


The CB supplies 3 power supplies to the passenger seat witchpack. The fused supplies provide power for the seat height and backrest recline, the seat forward/rearward and seat tilt and the head restraint and lumbar adjustment respectively. The B only provides the power to the passenger seat switch pack when the ignition is on (power mode 6).

For the seat movement and head restraint motors, when the applicable switch is operated, the power is supplied to the applicable side of the motor and the ground path is completed to operate the motor in the required direction. To move the motor in the opposite direction the polarity is reversed.

For the lumbar adjustment, when the switch is operated in the inflate position, power is supplied to the pump motor to inflate the lumbar support. When the switch is operated in the opposite direction, the power energizes a solenoid which in turn opens a valve to deflate the lumbar support.

On models with the passenger seat away switch, operation of the switch completes one of two ground paths to the passenger seat module. The module determines which ground path has been activated and operates the seat fore/aft motor in the applicable direction. The motor operates for as long as the switch is pressed or the motor reaches the fullrange of its adjustment.

The CB suppies 3 power supplies to the DSM and one supply to the driver seat switchpack.The fused supplies provide power for the movement motors in addtion to the driver seat switchpack. Power is permanently supplied to the DSM and the driver seat switchpack.

The driver seat switchpack is connected to the DSM by a LIN (local interconnect network) bus for the seat movement switches. Any selection for seat movement generates a message which is passed via the LIN to the DSM. The seat module processes the request and operates the appicable seat function as required using the power supplies from the CB.

Each seat motor contains a Hall position sensor. The sensor sends a feedback signal to the DSM. The signal is used for memory store and memory recall functions.

The lumbar adjustment switch on the driver seat switchpack is wired direct to the lumbar pump and solenoids. The switch, when moved t theiflatepoion fother the upper o lwer iflatale cushion cell provides a powersupply to the lumar pump and simultaneously activates the applicable inflate solenoid valve. When the switch is released, the pump stops and the solenoid valve closes trapping the ir in the ifatable cushion. When the switchis moved to the deflate position for either the upper or lower iflaable cushion cell power i supplied to theapplicable deflate solenoid valve which pens to allw the air in the cushion to escape. When the switch is released, the valve is closed and the remaining air in the cushion is retained.

The table below highlights the features available for each seating option.

![](images/_MISSING_08c693eb44275353be73210a04e74bbaf4d79bc01fe63cd6b47772e767a31d9d.jpg)

The 3-stage heated front seats feature 2 heater elements located in the seat cushion and a single heater element located in the seat backrest. Operation of the heated front seats i controlled by the ATC module via the TS, P and the  module on vehicles with heated seats. On vehicles with heated and cooled seats the operation is controlled by the TS, IP and the SCCM.

The heated and cooled front seats each contain 2 climate modules; one in the cushion, one in the backrest. The climate modules contain'Peltier' cell which are able to deliver heating and cooling based on a voltage provided by the SCM. Each climate modulealso contins a fan which blws air over the Pelter cell to ditriute heatedor cooledair via liners in the seat cushion and backrest. The fan is also controlled by the SCCM. The TSallows the driver and passenger to select 3 ranges of heated or coled ventilation: maximum, minimum and intermediate. Also, using the selections on the TS, the driver and passenger can select between full seat ventilation or backrest ventilation only.

Vehicles can be fitted with a heated steering whee independently of front seat options. For additional iformation, referto: (211-05 Steering Column Switches)

Steering Column Switches (Description and Operation), Steering Column Switches (Description and Operation), Steering Column Switches (Description and Operation).

Lumbar Support

On 10 and 14-way seats, a 2 way lumbar support is provided which allows the lumbar inflatable cushion to be inflated or deflated as required O 12, 16 and 18-way seats, a4 way lumar support ifitted which comprises wo separate cushion cell. The upper and lower cell can be ifated or deflatedividuall allwing greater comfort djustment fo the driver and passenger.

The lumbar support comprises an inflatable cushion located in the seat backrest, a pump and solenoids. The pump is activated when the applicable seat switch is moved to the inflate position, inflating the cels in the ilatable cushion. On  and 14-way seats, a single solenoid operated valve allws the inflatable cushion to be deflated. On12, 16 and 18-way seats, 4 solenoid valves control the iflation and deflation of the upper and lower inflatable cushion cells, allwing each cel to be adjusted individually.

The head restraint motor is located in the upper section of each seat backrest and is accessile by removal of the seat back. The motor moves a cradle which is driven in a vertical motion by a rack and pinion arrangement. The crade has the two head restraint stems attached to it and therefore, raises and lowers the head restraint as the motor moves the cradle. The motor contains a Hall sensor which supplies positional information to the DSM.

The seat forward/rearward motor is an integral component of the seat frame. The motor drives on a gear on a worm drive lead screw which is interal ith the floor rail. The lead screw has a stop at each end to limit the foreand aft seat movement.

The seat tilt motor i located below the seat. The seat it motor drivesa gear on a lead screw to raise the front of the seat cushion. The motor contains a Hall sensor which supplies positional information to the DSM.

The seat cushion extension motor is located below the seat. The motor drives a gear on a lead screw which extends or retracts the front of the seat cushion. The motor contains a Hall sensor which supplies positional information to the DSM.

The seat height motor is located below the seat. The seat height motor drives a gear on a lead screw. The lead screw moves lever mechanism which raises or lowers the seat cushion. The motor contains a Hal sensor which supplies positional information to the DSM.

The seat backrest recline motor is located in the seat back rest. The recline motor rotates a shaft which is connected the seat backrest frame and raises or lowers the back rest position. The motor contains a Hall sensor which supplies positional information to the DSM.

![](images/_MISSING_2c4a9fd259f9471a2ef8c8575a887acf3206ee509a65e45e6507e611f7f0deba.jpg)

On certain models a passenger seat away switch is fited to the inner bolster of the seat to allow the driver to move the passenger seat forwards or backwards to improve the rear legroom.

The two-way rocker switch allows the driver to move the front passenger seat forward or rearwards to adjust leg room for th rear seat passenger.

When a replacement DSM is fited it should be calibrated a Jaguar approved diagnostic system so that the module can learn the seats ábsolute position.

The rear seat features a single piece cushion and a fixed rear back with a 60/40 split backrest option. wo latches are seured to the rear bulkhead by a pair of  bolts to retain the seat backrests i the upright position.The latches can be released to fold down the individual cushions by pulling a cable release located below the rear window parcel shelf in the luggage compartment.

ISOFIX fastening points are attached to the vehicle floor to provide secure fastening for compatible child seats.

NOTE: Foldable rear seats on saloon vehicles are an optional fit

A centrall mounted center arm rest can be folded down from the fixed backrest, or from the 60% backrest. The arm rest contains two drink holders.

Leather is a natural product, therefore it bears natural characteristics, such as grain variations, growth & bush marks. These non-weakening marks show the true ature of the hide and are the hallmarks of Leather. In order to maintain the beauty of the vehiclesnatural Leather upholstery it requires regular cleaning, which if neglected, may cause deterioration. Where dust and dirt are allwed to accumulate and become ingrained in the surface of the Leather, the upholstery may become permanently damaged.

Light coloured upholstery can be particularly susceptile to soiling and staining and care should be taken to ensure that where there is evidence of any soilig or stining on the upholstery then this should be cleaned immediately using the Jaguar/Land Roverapproved productilure t dohis couldead t the stin becing permanent this appiet alleaher upholstery and is not colour specific.

Leather trimmed seats will naturall exhibit areas of creasing and wrinkling over a period of time and is a normal characteristic as the Leather ages.

Particular care should be taken where there is evidence of soiling or staining on the leather, this should be cleaned immediately. Failure to do this could lead to the stain becoming permanent.

Particular care should be taken to prevent damage from studs, zips and buckles.

The TS receivesa fused power suppy from the RB (rear junction box)After selecting the seat heating/limate seat menu on Integrated Control Panel (), ne of the threeseat heat temperature seletions made by the driver o passenger using the TS soft keys are passed from the TS on the medium speed CAN bus to the ICP. The ICP processes the information and transmits the request on the medium speed CAN bus to the ATC (automatic temperature control) module.

The seat cushion heater element has a thermal sensor which supplies a feedback signal back to the CB (central junction box The backrest heater elements do not have a thermal sensor and are maintained at the same temperature as the seat cushion elements.

The ATC module reacts to the driver request information received from the CP and requests the CB to activate the seat heaters. The C measures the returned temperature signals from the thermal sensors and relays the temperature signals back to the ATC module. The ATC module then uses the measured seat element temperatures to provide closed-loop control of the heater elements to maintain the temperature at one of the three heat ranges selected.

NOTE: To prevent excessive battery discharge, the heated front seats willonly operate when the engine is running.

The TS receives a fused power supply from the RJ .After selecting the seat heating/limate seat menu, selections made b the driver using the  soft keys are passedrom the  on the medum speed CN busto the P.The  processes the information and transmits the request on the medium speed CAN bus to the SCCM.

The SCCM receives its power supplies from the  .Heating and cooling requests are generated using the soft keys on the TS. These requests are transmitted to the P over the medium speed CAN bus. The ICP forwards these requests to the SCCM over the medium speed CAN bus.

The SCCM supplies power to the two climate modules in each seat. The temperature sensor in each climate module is monitored by the SCcM which uses the temperature information to control the Peltier cell acordingly and also the cooling fan motors to distribute the heated or cooled air.

NOTE: To prevent excessive battery discharge, the heated and cooled front seats wilonly operate when the engine is running.

The CB supplies 3 power supplies to the driver seat switchpack. The fused supplies provide power for the seat height and backrest recline, the seat forward/rearward and seat tit and the lumbar adjustment respectively. The  only provides the power to the driver seat switchpack when the ignition is on (power mode 6).

For the seat movement motors, when the applicable switch is operated, the power is suppled to the applicable side of the motor and the ground path is completed to operate the motor in the required direction.To move the motor in the opposite direction the polarity is reversed.

For the lumbar adjustment, when the switch is operated in the inflate position, power is supplied to the pump motor to inflate the lumbar support. When the switch is operated in the opposite direction, the power energizes a solenoid which in turn opens a valve to deflate the lumbar support.

The CB supplies 3 power supples to the passenger seat switchpack. The fused supplies provide power for the seat height and backrest recline, the seat forward/rearward and seat tilt and the head restraint and lumbar adjustment respectively. The CJB only provides the power to the passenger seat switch pack when the ignition is on (power mode 6).

For the seat movement and head restraint motors, when the applicable switch is operated, the power is supplied to the applicable side of the motor and the ground path is completed to operate the motor in the required direction. To move the motor in the opposite direction the polarity is reversed.

For the lumbar adjustment, when the switch is operated in the inflate position, power is supplied to the pump motor to inflate the lumbar support. When the switch is operated in the opposite direction, the power energizes a solenoid which in turn opens a valve to deflate the lumbar support.

On models with the passenger seat away switch, operation of the switch completes one of two ground paths to the passenger seat module. The module determines which ground path has been activated and operates the seat fore/aft motor in the

applicable direction. The motor operates for as long as the switch is pressed or the motor reaches the ful range of its adjustment.

The CB supplies 3 power supplies to the DSM and one supply to the driver seat switchpack. The fused supplies provide power for the movement motors i addition to the driver seat switchpack. Power is permanently supplied to the DSM and the driver seat switchpack.

The driver seat switchpack is connected to the DSM by a LIN (local interconnect network) bus for the seat movement switches. Any selection for seat movement generates a message which is passed via the LIN to the DSM. The seat module processes thé request and operates the appicable seat function as required using the power supplies from the CJB.

Each seat motor contains a Hal position sensor. The sensor sends a feedback signal to the DSM. The signal is used for memory store and memory recall functions.

The lumbar adjustment switch on the driver seat switchpack is wired direct to the lumbar pump and solenoids. The switch, when movedt the inflate potion foither the upper o lwer iflatablecushion cell provides a powersupply to the lmar pump and simultaneously activates the applicable inflate solenoid valve. When the switch is released, the pump stops and the solenoid valve closes trapping the air in the ifatable cushion. When the switchis moved to the deflate position for either the upper or lwer iflable cushion cell power i supplied to the applicable deflate solenoid valve which opens toallw the air in the cushion to escape. When the switch is released, the valve is closed and the remaining air in the cushion is retained.

On vehicles with heated and cooled seats the operation is controlled by the TS, IP and the SCCM.

The heated and cooled front seats each contain 2 climate modules; one in the cushion, one in the backrest. The climate modules contain'Peltier' cell which areable to deliver heating and cooling based on a voltage provided by the SCCM. Each climate modulealso contains a fan, which blows air verthe Pelter cell to distriute heated or cooledair via liners in the seat cushion and backrest. The fan i also controlled by the S. The  allws the driver and passenger to select  ranges o heated or coled ventilation: maximum, minimum and intermediate. Also, using the selections on the TS, the driver and passenger can select between full seat ventilation or backrest ventilation only.

The Passenger arbag is controlled by the RCM which chooses between single or dual stage deployment, depending on the occupant status and the crash severity. It consists of a two stage inflator with two air bag electrical connectors to accommodate the two stage inflation.

The heated gas iflator consists of a high-pressure mix of clean air and hydrogen gas, triggered by two separate ignition squibs. It produces a controlled generation of clean gas to rapidl fil the air bag. I i classied as a stored flammable gas (not asan explosive) and assuch, has less restrictive storage and transportation requirements. It produces a very clean burr and almost no particulates and is almost free of any toxins, making disposal or recycling much easier.

E144786

Side air curtains protect against head injuries in a side impact.

A single iflator mounted behind the rear seat unfurls the curtain and fil five separate chambers to provide head protection cushions for occupants in side-impact and roll-over events. Steel ramps guaranteethe curtain does not snag on the interior trim as it unfurls, while tethers at the front and rear of the curtain ensure the curtain is held taut.

![](images/_MISSING_61fc16460e69dd79e0ab4ac44254392b119d17f44463b46c5811c49a7e4a7e80.jpg)

E144787

A side air bag is attached to the outside of each front seat backrest frame, under the backrest cover.

The side air bags are handed and each consist of a fabric cover which contains the folded air bag and the infator. The seat harness conects the igniter of the inflator to a connector in the main seat harness conector block located under the front edge of the seat cushion.

When the air bag deploys it opens the fabric cover and splits open the backrest seat cover at the front sear

The side air bags use a solid propellant medium. The inflated volume of each side air bag is 20 liters.

![](images/_MISSING_8ae7c110939906b113c8e943ec5612f351b2cbb05a15f51195bb4fbbf5eae9f2.jpg)

The air bag warning indicator consists of a red Light Emitting Diode (LED) behind a SRS graphic in the instrument cluster.

Operation of the air bag warning indicator is controlled by a high speed CAN bus message from the RCM to the instrument cluster. The RCM sends the signal to illminate the air bag warning indicator if a fault is detected, and for approximately 6 seconds during the bulb check at the beginning of each ignition cycle.

The occupant classification system can determine if the front passenger seat is unoccupied, occupied by a small person, or occupied by a large person. The occupant classification system consists of:

A pressure pad, installed under the cushion of the front passenger seat, which is connected to a pressure sens A safety belt tension sensor, integrated into the anchor point of the front passenger safety belt An occupant classification module, installed under the front passenger seat.

he pressure pad is a silicone filled bladder. Any load on the pressure pad is detected by the pressure sensor.

The safety belt tension sensor is a strain gauge that measures the load applied by the safety belt anchor to the anchor bolt.   
The sensor is located in the lower safety belt anchor point.

### Portable Audio Interface Panel/USB Power Supply


The symptom chart indicates symptoms, sources and actions to address a condition.

Pinpoint Tests

For electrical systems, pinpoint test steps are used to identify the source of a concern in a logical, step-by-step manner.   
Pinpoint tests have two columns: CONDITIONS and DETAILS/RESULTS/ACTIONS.

The CONDITIONS column is used exclusively for graphics and icons (with or without captions) and the DETAILS/RESULTS/ACTIONS column provides direction to another test step or specific corrective actions.

The boxed numbers indicate the order in which the described action is to be carried out.

If DTC B1252-19 (USB Port General Electrical Failures - Circuit current above threshold) has been logged, the IAM has detected a current draw from the Portable Audio Interface Panel in excess of 1.7 Amps. In these circumstances, the power supply to the Portable Audio Interface Panel will be cut for an gnition cycle. To reset the system and restore power, the vehicle needs to be locked (with ignition off) and armed for at least 5 minutes.

The USB port n the Portable Audio Interface Panel is able to supply current to a maximum of 50mA. It should be noted that any portable devices connected via the USB port that required more power may not charge or power up correctly and that thi may affect the operation of this device with the infotainment system.

The Evaporative System Diagnostic Check routine will not run if the battery state of charge is too low. To proceed, connect the manufacturer approved Vehicle Battery Conditioner / Power Supply.

The Evaporative System Diagnostic Check routine wil not run if the fuel level is toolow (<15%).To proceed, ad the orrect grade of fuel as necessary.

The Evaporative System Diagnostic Check routine wil intilly measure the reference current drawn by the diagnosti module tank leakage pump, and then energise the changeover valve to pressurise the fuel tank. The combustible gas detector i then used to identify the source of a leak. The routine takes approximately 10 minutes may be performed up to 3 times to allow time to test the entire fuel system.

Perform the following steps to test the combustible gas detector:

1.Rotate the sensitivity control full counter-clockwise   
2. Set the combustible gas detector power switch to 'ON'   
Check the battery warning indicator - The batteries must be recharged if the warning indicator is not iluminated   
4. Allow the combustible gas detector to warm up (approximately 30 seconds)   
Slowly rotate the sensitivity control full clockwise - Check that the ticking rate increases and ultimately becomes a   
siren   
6When testing is complete, set the combustible gas detector power switch to 'OFF'

CAUTIONS:

Adischarged battery condition may have been caused by anelectrical short circuit. If this condition exists there wil be anapparentl ive ciruit on the ehicle en whenalircut areitchedofThisan causearig whenthe jump eads are connected.

Whilst it is not recommended that the vehicle is jump started it is recognized that this may ocasionally be the only practical ay oilie a eiclech an istance the dichare baty must eechargdmmeiatel afer jump starting to avoid permanent damage.

Always make sure that the jump leads are adequate for the task. Heavy duty cables must be used.   
Always make sure that the slave battery is of the same voltage as the vehicle battery.The batteries must be connected in parallel.   
Always make sure that switchable electric circuits are switched off before connecting jump leads. This reduces the risk of sparks occurring when the final connection is made.

![](images/_MISSING_3e68953d9b9fbe369e8ce4f6c8e93d09d7858576956980610b70d170e2713439.jpg)

ARninG: Make sure that the ends o the jump leads do not touch each other or ground aginst the vehicle body a any time whilethe lead aretached tthe battery. fully charged battery, if shorted trough jump leadscan dischargeat a rate well above 100 amps causing violent arcing and very rapid heating of the jump leads and terminals, and can even cause the battery to explode.

Always connect the jump leads in the following sequence.

Slave battery positive first then vehicle battery positive.

Slave battery negative next and then vehicle ground at least, 300 mm (12 in from the battery terminal e.g. engine lifting bracket.

Always reduce the engine speed to idle before disconnecting the jump leads.

Before removing the jump leads, switch on the heater blower (high) or the heated rear screen, to reduce the voltage peak when the leads are rémoved.

Always disconnect the jump leads in the reverse order to the connecting sequence and take great care not to short the ends of the leads.

Do not rely on the generator to restore a discharged battery. For a generator to recharge a battery, it would take inexcess of 8 hours continuous driving with no additional loads placed ón the battery.

Ensure adequate ventilation.

Many of the materials found on or associated with the repair of vehicles are highly flammable. Some give offtoxic or harmful fumes if burnt.

Observe strict fire safety when storing and handling flammable materials or solvents, particularly near electrical equipment or welding processes.

Ensure, before using electrical or welding equipment, that there is no fire hazard present.

Have a suitable fire extinguisher available when using welding or heating equipment.

Before working on or in the vicinity of SRS components, make sure the system is rendered safe by performing the following operations:

Remove the ignition key.

The electri rear diffential has the same functionality as the pen rear differential, but it also incorporates a locking and torque biasing function to give improved traction performance and vehicle dynamic stability. Operation of the electric rear differential is controlled by the Rear Differential Control Module (RDCM).

Vehicles from 14MY : V S/ 5.0L Petrol model from 14MY are fited with a modified electric rear differential. The main differential remains unchanged, however the diffrential locking motor and the reduction gear casing are modified.

The basic construction of the electric rear differential is similar to the open rear differential. However, the electric rear differential also has the follwing:

Two additional planet gears in the differential carrier, to cater for the higher torque through the differential during locking events.   
A multi-plate clutch and actuator assembly installed on the left sun gear   
A motor and reduction gearbox, attached to the cover.   
Atemperature sensor installed in the cover.

The RDCM operates the motor of the electri rear diffrential under the control of the Integrated Suspension Control module (ISCM).

Exploded View of Electric Rear Differential - Up To 14MY

![](images/_MISSING_b214adba6bb95b9f1f7f41b7478af644beac8b62c5181d4aa39b6ef7b5b03bfb.jpg)

E105859   
![](images/_MISSING_2e1e6b714c33be3c9f14387ddacf8ae13824aa04e9e80bb57e600e3174cdf941.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_2eae30c333dfd171c80ce29f1c9f3592c7f3666d2c240a80beeca42eb71fb08f.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_ddbde41586ab253492936ceadaf8ade7bda20630cf3b0005035c31fc77339592.jpg)

E156379   
![](images/_MISSING_2cb3fef99af18899529262f568b495433f5cec1a711e29430a102685dc156589.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_46c1549d8576ace66d483a4e01ac28d8f523b9ef0800d27ac857b5dfc2327406.jpg)
The multi-plate clutch is contained in a clutch basket attached to the differential carrier with the crown wheel securing bolts. Alternate plates of the clutch pack are keyed to the cutch basket and the left sun gear.A pressure dsc is installed on the outer end of the clutch pack and keyed to the clutch basket. A thrust race on the end of the clutch basket incorporates lugs which extend through the clutch basket onto the pressure disc.

The actuator assembly is mounted on bearings on the utboard end of the clutch basket, against the thrust race.The actuator assembly cosist onput and utut actators separated by five bal bearings.A lcking pi in the cover engaes with aslt in the output actuator to prevent it turning, but allow it to move axially.The iput actuator engages with the reduction gearbox and i free to rotate relative to the cover.Bal bearings locatein curved grooves in the mating faces ofthe iput and output actuators. The bottom surface of each groove incorporates a ramp. Rotation of the input actuator forces the ball bearings up the ramps in the grooves and induces an axial movement in the output actuator. The thrust race and pressure disc transfer the axial movement from the output actuator to the clutch pack.

![](images/_MISSING_15961b6ea924f14e38d2d0a22e83523e546abe7c615f84dae6b039378254bd39.jpg)

E112539   
![](images/_MISSING_6c0bf1718453a79dffdb75c39cd343ee2ab2df4b5fd14a5a8a7662b32e6a906f.jpg)

The differential locking motor sa2 DC motor that adjusts the frictional lading of the multi-plateclutch, via the reduction gearbox and the actutor assembly, under the control of the RDCM. Adjusting the frictional ading of the multi-plate clutch adjusts the locking torque between the crown wheel drive gear and the sun wheel.

Four bolts attach the motor to the reduction gearbox, which is located in position on the cover with two dowels, and secured with four bolts. An O-ring seals the joint between the motor and the reduction gearbox.

he motor is driven by a 12 V DC feed direct from the RDCM. The motor also incorporates the following connections with the DCM

A motor temperature sensor, to prevent excessive use from damaging the motor.   
Two Hall effect motor position sensors, to enable closed loop control of the motor.

The temperature sensor provides a diferential oil temperature signal to the RDCM, to prevent excessive use from damaging the multi-plate clutch.

High-pitched buzzing sound, like an electric motor or drill

The Evaporative System Diagnostic Check routine wil not run if the battery state of charge is too low. To proceed, connect the manufacturer approved Vehicle Battery Conditioner / Power Supply.

The Evaporative System Diagnostic Check routine wil not run if the fuel level is too low <15%). To proceed, add the orrect grade of fuel as necessary.

The Evaporative System Diagnostic Check routine wil itially measure the reference current drawn by the diagnostic module tank leakage pump, and then energise the changeover valve to pressurise the fuel tank. The combustible gas detector i then used to identify the source of a leak. The routine takes approximately 0 minutes may be performed up to 3 times to allow time to test the entire fuel system.

Perform the following steps to test the combustible gas detector:

Rotate the sensitivity control fully counter-clockwise   
Set the combustible gas detector power switch to 'ON'   
Check the battery warning indicator - The batteries must be recharged if the warning indicator is not iluminated   
4. Allow the combustible gas detector to warm up (approximately 30 seconds)   
Slowly rotate the sensitivity control full clockwise - Check that the ticking rate increases and ultimately becomes a   
siren   
When testing is complete, set the combustible gas detector power switch to 'OFF'

Diesel fuel is dawn from the tank by the internal electric ft pump.The fuel pressure regulator located in the fuel pump module assembly regulates the delivery pressure at approximately .5 bar to the transfer pump housed in the High Pressure (HP) pump. A VCV (volume control valve) governs the amount of fuel supplied to the HP pump.

The transfer and high pressure pump are driven directly by the engine. Due to the storage volume of the common rail, the injection pressure will remain practically constant over the complete duration of the injection process.

The HP pump has a return pipe circuit which is separate from the injector return pipes. Ree Fuel Charig d Controls(03-4A Fuel Charing and Contros- TV . Diesel Descipti and peration

At closed or partill open trottle positions, the electric by-pass valve actuator i fully open, allwing a flow of air from the superchargeroutlet, back to the net side. This results i litte or no pressure increase across the supercharger. Progressive opening of the throttle reduces the depression downstream of the electric throttleThis issensed by the Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor in the electric throttle housing and the Temperature and Manifold Absolute Pressure (TMAP) sensor in the rear ft side of the supercharger eft intercooler.Signals from these sensors are recived by the Engine Control Module (ECM), which operates the by-pass valve actuator to close the valve. As the by-pass valve closes there is a coresponding increase in the outlet pressure from the supercharger, which increases engine power output.

Electrical power for the charge air coolant pump is supplied from the intercoler coolant pump relay n the E When the intercooler coolant pump rely is energized it connects power from the battery to the charge aircoolant pump. Operation of the intercooler coolant pump relay is controlled by the EM. The intercooler coolant pump relay is energized continuously while the ignition is in power mode 6.

When the charge air coolant pump is running, coolant flows from the pump outlet through the charge air coolers, the charge air radiator and back to the pump inlet.

The Mechatronic valve block is located in the bottom of the transmission and is covered by the fluid pan. The valve block houses the TM , electrical actuators, speed sensors, control valves and the hydraulic impulse storage which provide all electro-hydraulic control for al transmission functions. The Mechatronic valve block comprises the following components:

ТСм   
Seven pressure regulator solenoids Two park lock solenoids   
Twenty one hydraulic spool valves Température sensor   
Turbine speed sensor   
Output shaft speed sensor   
Hydraulic impulse storage.

Valve Block Components

![](images/_MISSING_c4a485ee8db9fd0252c7c9cf8c8f443ab7983f82138a5a59c754c387e67ce347.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_1b96de3b98dd8919f043e8ce173432076b8ad38238942c45b91f554157cb9d01.jpg)
Electronic Pressure Regulator Solenoids (EPRS)

![](images/_MISSING_18cd396fad31800a61faf66ead2c80a98c6733eb9ffbd8f5b0ae2132a692579a.jpg)

Seven EPRS are lcated in the valve block.The solenoids are controld by PWM signals from the TM . The solenoids convert the electrical signals into hydraulic control pressure proportional to the signal to actuate the spool valves for precise transmission operation.

Solenoids EPRS A, B, D, Eand W supply a higher control pressure as the sigal amperage increases and can be identified by an orange connector cap. The TCM operates the solenoids using PWM signals. The TM monitors engine lad and clutch slip and varies the solenoid duty cycle acordingly. The solenoids have a 12  operating voltage and a pressure range of 0 -4.7 bar (0 - 68 Ibf.in 2 ).

Solenoids EPRs  and SYs suppy a lower control pressure as the signal amperage increases and can be identified by a gray connector cap. The TCM monitors engine load and clutch slip and varies the solenoid duty cycle accordingly. The solenoids have a 12 V operating voltage and a pressure range of 4.7 - 0 bar (68 - 0 Ibf.in ² .

The resistance of the solenoid coil winding for EPRS solenoids is 5.05 Ohms at 20 °C (68 F).

The ignition coils are supplied with electrical power from the battery via a 250 A megafuse in the BB, a 500A megafuse behind the instrument panel and the iitionrelay in the E.The control signal for the igition relay is suppied by the EM

The ECM sends a separate signal to each iition coil to trigger the power stagewitching. The EM calulates the dwel time from the battery voltage and engine speed to ensure a costant energy level i produced in the secondary coil each time the power stage is witched.This ensures sufficient spark energy is availale without excessive primary current flow, which avoids overheating and damage to the ignition coils.

The ECM calculates the ignition timing for individual cylinders from:

Engine speed   
Camshaft position   
Engine load   
Enine temperature   
The knock control function   
The shift control function   
The idle speed control function.

т WARNINg: Servicing must be carred out by personnel familiar with both vehicle system and the charging and testing equipment. All operations must be carried out in á well ventilated area away from open flame and heat sources.

CAUTION: Diagnosis by substitution from a donor vehicle is NoT acceptable. Substitution of control modules does not guarantee cofirmation of a fault, and may also cause aditional faults in the vehicle being tested and/or the donor vehicle.

NOTES:

If a control module or a component is suspect and the vehicle remains under manufacturer warranty, refer to the Warranty Policy andProcedures manual or determine if any prior approval programme operationpriorto the istalltion of a new module/component.

When performing voltage or resistance tests, always use a digital multimeter accurate to three decimal places, and with an up-to-date calibration certificate. When testing resistance always take the resistance of the digital multimeter leads into account.

Check and rectify basic faults before beginning diagnostic routines involving pinpoint tests.

Check DDW for open campaigns. Refer to the corresponding bulletins and SSMs which may be valid for the specific customer complaint 'and carry out the recommendations as required

A BATTERY CELLS CONTAIN SULPHURIC ACID AND EXPLOSIVE MIXTURES OF HYDROGEN AND OXYGEN GASES. IT IS THEREFORE ESSENTIAL THAT THE FOLLOWING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS ARE OBSERVED.

Batteries emit highly explosive hydrogen at alltimes, particularly during charging.To prevent any potential form of gnition occurring when working in the vicinity of a battery:

Do not smoke when working near batteries.   
Avoid sparks, short circuits or other sources of ignition in the battery vicinity.   
Switch off current before making or breaking electrical connections.   
Ensure battery charging area is well ventilated.   
Ensure the charger is switched off when: a connecting to a battery; b disconnecting from the battery.   
Always disconnect the ground cable from the battery terminal first and reconnect it last.

Batteries contain poisonous and highly corrosive acid.To prevent personal injury, or damage to clothing or the vehicle, eoli rig pracieule folle etppipcheglcrlteeiiravyreaefit carrying batteries:

Always wear suitable protective clothing (an apron or similar), safety glasses, a face mask and suitable gloves. If acid is spilld or splashed onto clothing or the body, it must be neutralized immediately and then rinsed with clean water. A solution of baking soda or household ammonia and water may be used as a neutralizer. In the event of contact with the skin, drench the affected area with water. In the case of contact with the eyes, bathe the affected area with cool clean water for approximately 15 minutes and seek urgent medical attention. If battery acid is spiled or splashed on any surface of a vehicle, it should be neutralized and rinsed with clean water. Heat is generated when acid is mixed with water. If it becomes necessary to prepare electrolyte of a desired specific gravity, SLowLY pour the concentrated acid into water (not water into acid), adding small amounts of acid while stirring. Allow the electrolyte to cool if noticeable heat develops. With the exception of lead or lead-lined containers, always use non-metallc receptacles or funnels. Do not store acid in excessively warm locations or in direct sunlight.
