### Occupant Detection System


![](images/_MISSING_3320ed8820cdcc311245858afa9c51877739f80cdaedcb59f58c6fe99bebdd15.jpg)

In acolision, the sudden deceleration or aceleration is measured by the impact sensors and the accelerometers in the RCM. The RCM evaluates the readings to determine the impact point on the vehicle and whether the deceleration/aceleration readings exceed the limit for firing any of the ir bags, pretensioners, and battery disconnect unit. During a collion, the RCM only fires the air bags and pretensioners if the saving function confirms that the data from the impact sensor(s) indicates an impact limit has been exceeded.

The RCM incorporates the following impact thresholds to cater for different accident scenarios:

Front impact, pretensioners Front impact, driver and passenger air bags stage 1, belt unfastened Front impact, driver and passenger air bags stage 1, belt fastened Front impact, driver and passenger air bags stage 2, belt unfastened Front impact, driver and passenger air bags stage 2, belt fastened Rear impact Driver side impact Passenger side impact.

The front impact thresholds increase in severity from pretensioners, through to driver and passenger air bag stage 2, belt fastened.

There are two types of occupant monitoring:

In all markets except NAS & Australia, vehicles have an occupant detection sensor In NAS markets, vehicles have an occupant classification system

For markets which have an occupant detection sensor, this has no interface with the restraints system and only provides th belt reminder function.

For markets that have an occupant classfiation system, this provides the RCM with the occupancy status of the front passenger seat. The RM uses this and the seat buckle status i the evlation of the fring stratey for the passenger front air bag, side air bag, and pretensioner.

The buckle of each front safety belt incorporates a Halleffect sensor that provides a safety belt status signal to the RCM. The RCM broadasts the status of the two front safety belts on the high speed CAN bus for use by the instrument cluster. In the event of a front impact the RM wil deploy the pretensioners provided the safety belt buckles are fastened. The safety belt buckle pretensioners have a lower deployment threshold than that required by the air bags. Hence it is possible during a minor collsion, which exceeds the deployment threshold, that only the safety belt buckle pretensioners wil deploy.

There are two types of occupant monitoring:

•In all markets except NAS & Australia, vehicles have an occupant detection sensor In NAS markets, vehicles have an occupant classification system

For markets which have an occupant detection sensor, this has no interface with the restraint system and only provides the belt reminder function.

For markets that have an occupant classfiation system, this provides the RCM with the occupancy status of the front passenger seat. The RCM uses this and the seat bucke status i the evlation of the fring strategy for the passenger front air bag, side air bag, and pretensioner.

![](images/_MISSING_a1642715144b58c0b6906832e0472cbcded788e4173ea579cdbb9a11064af949.jpg)

The occupant classfication module supplies a rference voltae to the pressure sensor and the safety belt tension sensor and, from the returned signals, measures the lads acting on the pressure pad and the safety belt tension sensor. The load measurement from the safety belt tension sensor is used to produce a corection factor for the load measurement from the pressure pad.The thtess of the safety belt affects the load acting on the pressure pad, so without the corection facto the occupant classification module cannot derive an accurate occupancy status.

The occupant classfication module translates the load readings into a seat occupancy status and transmits the result to the RCM, on a dedicated high speed CAN bus link. The occupant classification module incorporates two load limits for the seat cushion: When the loadexceedsthe lower limit, but is less than the upper limit, the ccupant is classified as mall; when the upper limit is exceeded, the occupant is classified as large.

### Transfer Case Clutch Calibration Angle Results Table


CAUTION: Diagnosis by substitution from a donor vehicle is NoT acceptable. Substitution of control modules does not guarantee confirmation of a fault, and may also cause aditional faults in the vehicle being tested and/or the donor vehicle

NOTES:

f the control module or a component is suspect and the vehicle remains under manufacturer warranty, refer to the warranty policy and procedures manual, or determine if any prior approval programme is in operation, prior to the installation of a new module/component

Generic scan tools may not read the codes listed, or may read only 5-digit codes. Match the 5 digit from the scan tool to the first  digit of the 7-dgit code listed to identify the fault (the last  digits give extra information read by the manufacturer-approved diagnostic system)

When performing voltage or resistance tests, always use a digital multimeter accurate to three decimal places and with acurrent calibration certificate. When testing resistance, always take the resistance of the digital multimeter leads into account

Check and rectify basic faults before beginning diagnostic routines involving pinpoint tests

Inspect connectors for signs of water ingress, and pins for damage and/or corrosion

f DTs are recorded and, after performing the pinpoint tests, a faultis not present, an intermittent concern may be the cause. Always check for loose connections and corroded terminals

f the rear differential control module, rear differential locking motor or the rear differential are replaced, the on demand self test (ODsT) must be carried out to calibrate the components

Where an 'o demand self-test' is referred to, this can be accessed via the 'DTC monitor' tab on the manufacturers approved diagnostic system

Check DDW for open campaigns. Refer to the corresponding bulletins and SSMs which may be valid for the specific customer complaint and carry out the recommendations as required

The five most important sources of non-axle noise are exhaust,tres, roo racks, trim and mouldings, and transmission.

Therefore, make sure that none of the following conditions are the cause of the noise before proceeing with a driveline tea down and diagnosis.

Under certain conditions, the pitch of the exhaust may sound very much like gear noise. At other times, it can be mistaken for a wheel bearing rumble Tires, especially snow tires, can have a high pitched tread whine or roar, similar to gear noise. Radial tires, to some degree, have this characteristic. Also, any non-standard tire with an unusual tread construction may emit a roar or whine type noise   
Trim and mouldings can also cause whistling or a whining noise

Clunk may be a metalli noise heard when the automatic transmission is engaged in reverse or drive, or it may occu when the throttle is applied or released. It is caused by backlash somewhere in the driveline Bearing rumble sounds like marbles being tumbledThis condition is usual caused by a damaged wheel bearing

The two-piece driveshaft, manufactured from lightweight tubular stee, transmits drive from the engine, via the transmission, to the diffrential. The driveshaft aligns with the centerline of the vehicle's body and is supported by a center bearing.

The driveshaft' front tube is of swaged construction, which is a crash energy management feature, designed to collapse progressively and predictably in the event of a severe frontal impact. A low-friction splined slip-joint at the center of the driveshaft provide the driveshaft's plunge capability.

Flexible couplings connecting the driveshaft to both the transmission and the diffrential counteract the angular movement the driveshaft caused by the driveline's acceleration and braking forces.

The center universal joint is positioned at a specified angle using shims between the center bearing and the vehicle's body. The driveline angles have been carefully configured to balance minimum power losses with excellent vibration and wear characteristics. The universal joint is lubricated during manufacture and sealed for life.

Rotational iput from the front driveshaft is passed vi the input flage to the piion shaft and pinion gear.The angles ofthe pinion gear to the crown wheel drive gear moves the rotational direction through 90°.

The transferred rotational motion is passed to the crown wheel drive gear, which in turn rotates the diffrential carrier. A shaft, which is secured to the carrer, rotates at the same speed as the carrier. The planet gears, which are mounted on the shaft alo rotate with the carrer. turn, the planet gears transfer their roatioal motionto the eft nd right snwheels, rotating the left and right halfshafts.

When the vehile is moving in a forward direction, the torque applied through the iffrential t each sunwheelis equal. In this condition both halfshaft rotate at the same speed.The planet gears do not rotate and effectively lock the sunwheels to the carrier.

f the veicle iturning, the outer veicle whee wil be forced to rotate fasterthan the iner vicle wheel by haing a greate distance to travel.The iffrential senses the torque iference between the sunwhel.The planet gears rotate on their axes to allow the outer vehicle wheel to rotate faster than the inner one.

The diffrential case comprises two halves with machined mating faces. When assembled, the case halves are sealed and secured together with 10 bolts.A breather is fitted to the case which prevents the ingress of water when the vehicle is wadingg.

The left caseifitted with a drain plug and fil/evel plug. The front differential unit contains approximately .295 liter (0.51 pint UK) of oil for a dry fill.

The diffrential is a conventional design using a hypoid gear layout. This employs a hypoid bevel pinion gear and crown wheel, with the pinion offetaove the centreline of the rwn wheel. This deig llows for a larger piion gear to be used which has the advantages of increased gear strength and reduced operating noise.

The diferential comprises a pinion shaft and hypoid bevel gear, a crown wheel drive gear with an integral carrier, which houses two planet gears. Two sunwheels are also located in the carrier and pass the rotational drive to the halfshafts.

The pinion shaftis mounted on two opposed bearings; one taper rollr bearing and one angular contact bearing, with a collapsible spacer located between them. The spacer is used to hold the bearing in aligment and also colpses under the pressure applied to the pinion nut. This allows the bearing preload to be set without the use of selectable shims.

The pinion shaft has an external splined outer end which accepts and locates the input flange, which is retained by the pinion nut.The pposite end of the output flange provides positive location for the front driveshaft. An oil seal is pressed into the left caing and sealthe put fag to theifent unitThe iio shaft as hypo bevel arat innered which mates with the crown wheel drive gear.

The crow wheel drive gear is welded onto the carrier. The carrier is mounted on taper rolle bearings located in each case halfThe bearings are pressfitted into the case anda spacer is located on the outsideface to set backlash and apply preload to the bearing.

The carrer is fited with a shaft onto which the two planet gears are mounted.The shaft is secured in the carrer with a roll pin. The sunwheels are located in pockets within the carrier and mesh with the planet gears. Thrust washers are located between the carrier and the sunwheels and hold the sunwheels in mesh with the planet gears. Each sunwheel has a machined, splined, bore to accept the drive shaft.A groove is machined in the bore to locate the snap ring fited to the drive shaft, providing positive drive shaft location.

Rotational input from the drive shaf i passed via the input flange to the pinion shaft and pinion gear. The angles of the pinion gear to the crown wheel drive gear moves the rotational direction through 90°.

The transferred rotational motion is now passed to the crown wheel drive gear, which in turn rotates the diffrential casing. The cross-shaft which is seured to the casing, also rotates at the same speed as the casing. The planet gears, which are mounted on the shaft, also rotate with the casing. In turn, the planet gears transfer their rotational motion to the let and right hand sun gears, rotating the drive halfshafts.

When the vehicle is moving in a forward dirction, the torque applied through the diffrential to each sun gear iequal. nthi condition both drive halfshafts rotate at the same speed and the planet gears do not rotate.

If the vehicle i turning, the outer wheel wil be forced to rotate faster than the inner wheel by having a greater dstance to travel. The differential senses the torque difference between the sun gears.The planet gears rotate on their axes to allow the outer wheel to rotate faster than the inner one.

The multi-plate clutch prevents excessive differential slip and therefore maximizes the traction performance of the vehicle. This i fundamentally different from braked' traction control systems, which can only counteract differential slip when it occurs.

A certain amount of diffential slip i required to allow the vehicle to turn corners and to remain stable under control of the ABS (anti-lock brake system)  The system is completely automatic and does not require any special driver input.

The multi-plate clutch actively controls the torque flow through the differential and optimizes the torque distribution in the driveline.The clutch biases the torque from the iferential to the wheel with the higher grip and prevent the whee with the lower grip from spinning.

OPEN REAR DIFFERENTIAL - V6 3.0L S/C PETROL, GTDi 2.OL PETROL AND TDV6 3.0L DIESEL VEHICLES

![](images/_MISSING_28b2e3197e1970efefcda333ab2f8bda19bfa18bc68c50487c5c571b02427545.jpg)
The open rear iffrentialis a conventional design using a hypoid gear layout. The final drive ratios diffe between engine ype, refer to Overview for ratio details.

The cast iron casing comprises two parts; a cover and a carrer.The carrier provides locations for al the internal components The oversaledt the arrier with Loctie sealant and seured with nine boltThe cover and carriehaeast is which assist rigidity and cooling. A breather cap is fitted to the top of the carrier.

The diesel pen rear diffential ifers from the petrol variant in respect to the final drive ratio and the iput flage which connects the propshaft to the differentialThe diesel input flange is larger to address driveline N (noise, vibration and harshness) boom inherent with the diesel engine.

Exploded View of Open Rear Differential

![](images/_MISSING_e17c04391fad3ff9ec08af2e9cb938285042adc881e033c9003627aa227056e5.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_945c2abaf5fba555dadf2e1b8ca1c7b004fe66cddbf21ce8353d23610663a24d.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_340f4d8c11d48614bb474eada148b03ec9819fdd1f6cc6667efd88311953f4f9.jpg)
The open rear diffrential contains a quantity of oil for splash lubrication of the internal components. A magnetic drain plug is installed in the bottom of the carrier and a filler/level plug is installed in the cover.

The open rear differential comprises a pinion shaft and hypoid pinion gear, and a crown wheel drive gear attached to a differential carrier. The differential carrier houses two planet gears and two sun gears

The pinion shaft has an externll splined outer end, which accepts and locates the input flange, which is retained by the pinion nut. The input flange has six threaded holes for the driveshaft attachment bolt.An oil seal is pressed into the carrie to seal the iput flage to the carrer.The pinion shaft has a hypoid gear at  ner end which mates with the crow wheel drive gear.

The crown wheel drive gear is located on the differential carrier and seured with ten bolt.The differential carrie i mounted on taper rller bearings located in machined bores in the carier and the cover. Shims are installed behind the bearing cups to apply the correct bearing preload and hypoid backlash.

The diffrential carrier has a through hole, which provides location for a cross shaft.The planet gears are installed on the cross shaft, with thrust washers between the planet gears and the differential arrier. A rol pin locks the cross shaft to the differential carrier.

The sun gears are located in pockets i the diffrential carrier and mesh with the planet gears. Belile washers are fitted between the sun gears and the differential carrier and set the corret mesh contact between the planet gears and the sun gears. Each sun gear has a machined bore with internal splines and a machined groove. The splines transfer drive to the rear drive halfshafts. The groove provides positive location for the snap ring fitted to the inboard end of the rear drive halshafts.

Oil seals are installed in the carrier and the cover to seal the rear drive halfshafts.

For additional information, refer to the relevant description and operation section of the workshop manual. REFER to: Rear Drive Axle and Differential (205- Rear Drive Axle/Differential Description and Operation)

The TM (transmission control module) changes the shif maps for the JaguarDrive Control mode selected. This changes the shift points providing early or late upshits and downshift. For example, on slippery surfaes i Winter mode the transmission will select 2nd gear for starting from a standstill on a flat surface to minimize wheel slip.

### Transfer Case - Transfer Case Front Output Seal Removal and Installation


The Automatic Speed Limiter (ASL) is activated by pressing the ASL switch on the transmission control switch control module.   
A second press of the switch will de-activate the ASL.

The operation of the ASL is similar to the standard speed control system with the following differences:

The outer marker on the speedometer in the instrument cluster showing the ASL set speed is shown in an amber color   
ressing and holding theETt'switch willicrease the ALspeed i icrement o km/hmph), a ingle press wil increase speed in 1 km/h (1 mph) increments Pressing the accelerator pedal fully to initiate kickdown, will ancel the ASL function and give full vehicle speed control back to the driver   
The message "Limiter Cancelled" will be displayed in the instrument cluster together with an audible notification.

ASL will not occu when resuming ASL after a cancel has occured, if the vehicle speedis noticeably different to set speed.

The transfer case is a'torque on demand' coupling, which is controld by a Transfer Case Control Module (TCM). The unit is manufactured by Magna.

The transfer case can adjust the driveline output from Rear Wheel Drive (RWD) to Al Wheel Drive (AWD) depending on driving style and road surface conditions.

The TCCM is located on the underside of the transfer case.The TCM is conected on the high speed Controlle Area Network (CAN) bus and receives data from various control modules including the Engine Control module (ECM) and the Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) control module. Using information from other control modules the TCCM can determine the required torque to be applied to the front wheels via an electronically controlled clutch and gear drive to the front driveshaft.

The driver can indirectly select AWD setings through selection ofthe Jaguar Drive Control (DC) modes (normal mode, winter mode and dynamic mode).

TRANSFER CASE

![](images/_MISSING_0241f8bb04a0e99b9c03e487fdeec5617c569bb377f73327761c92e9ba691d9c.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_c6b297f39f10efc0b27f1ac453cc15190614b4608b6c360de95b3faf15573e83.jpg)
The transfer case includes a multi-plate wet clutch, electro-mechanical actuation, and a gear driven front output. The system ensures high dynamic torque distribution between front and rear wheels.

The transfer case is mounted on the rear of the automatic transmission housing and is also supported on a subframe atached to the vehicle body. The subframe is attached to the vehicle body with four bolts.

A mounting bush is attached to the right side of the transfer case and is secured to the subframe. The bush, along with two snubbers, provides damping for vibrations in the driveline. A mass damper is attached to the rear of the transfer case to further improve Noise, Vibration and Harshness (NVH).

The transfer case comprises two casing halves, bolted together and sealed with a gasket. The casings house bearings in which the input shaft, intermediate gear and front output shaft run.

The input shaft passes through the two casings and is attached by a flange to the rear driveshaft. This provides 100% drive to the rear wheels only when the multiplate clutch is disengaged.

The multiplate clutch comprises an inner drive hub, an outer basket and set of drive plates and friction plates. The drive plates are located on splines on the input shaft and rotate at al time whenthe input shaft is rotating.The frictio plates are loated i grooves in the outer cltch basket which is positively atched to the front drive gear. The front drive gear and outer clutch basket are located on bearings to allow speed difference relative to the input shaft when no locking torque is applied. When the vehicle is moving, the front driveshaft, the front driveshaft output flange and output drive gear, the itermediate gearand the front drive gear and outer clutch basket allrotate.Torque is not applied to the front driveshaft until the CM engages the multiplate clutch.

The ball ramp assembly is located on extensions to the casings and is stationary and does not rotate with the input shaft. The ball ramp comprises two plates with opposing tapered grooves, into which a hardened steel ballis located. One of the ball ramp plates isattached to a pressure plate which acts directly on the multiplate clutch. The second plate has an annular gear ring which is driven by the worm drive of the TCM actuator. When the second plate is rotated by the actuator and worm drive, the steel balls are forced up the tapered grooves. This causes the first plate to move axially and appy pressure to the multiplate clutch via the presure plate.The amount of pressure applied is dependent on the rotation of the annular gear on the second plate and is controlled by the TCM. This variable adjustment ofthe ballramp allows ifinite adjustment of the torque loading through the clutch and the amount of torque applied through the gears to the front output shaft flange.

The casings have a drain plug and a level plug, which lw the oil level in the unt to be checked or replaced i line with the service schedule.

![](images/_MISSING_b7f70cc60f3cac955e7a52f5b10126042ab06b6ca4d71e6592d886f0fc58657b.jpg)

E145801

The TCCM controls the operation of the 'on demand' multiplate clutch. The TCCM is located on the underside of the transfer case and is secured with'two bolts.

The TCCM receives two power supplies via an AWD relay located in the Engine Junction Box (E) for TCCM logic and actuator supply, an igition suppy via the ignition relay in the Central Junction Box (C) for system wake-up and a shared ground with the Transmission Control Module (TCM). A high speed CAN (controller area network) bus connection connects the TCCM with the ABS (anti-lock brake system) control module, ECM (engine control module) and other vehicle systems.

The TCCM contains an actuator which is controlled by the TCCM using data from other system modules. The actuator rotates worm drive which in turn rotates a gear attached to the ballramp mchanism which applies axial lading to the multiplate clutch. The TCM control the torque applied to the front wheels by controling the axial loading applied to the multiplate clutch in response to information from other system modules. The TCM can llw a certain amount of 'slip' through the clutch to control the perentage of drive applied to the front driveshaft. f the CM target 100% lock-up of the clutch, the output speed wil be equal to the front and rear differentials. The torque distributed depends on the vilble traction at the wheels which will otate at the same speed but with different torque, depending on driving conditions. The TCCM can only control the drive to the front driveshaft, the drive to the rear driveshaft is direct from the transmission through the transfer case and is always directly driven.

If the TCM targets 100% lock-up of the clutch then the speed willbe matched between front and rear axles and torque distributed depending on available traction at the wheels same speed, but different torque - depending on driving condition

The TCCM outputs data on the high speed CAN bus to other system modules to advise the status of the multiplate clutch application.

If the TCM is unable to operate the on demand multiplate clutch correcty, it issue a message on the high speed CAN bus which is displayed in the istrument cluster message center as WheeDrive Only. Traction Reduced'.The CM willdisable the actuator and the transfer case will operate in RWD only.

IfaTC (diagnostic trouble code i stored relating t input voltage failure or high speed CAN bus failure, the vehicle harness, connectors and other system modules must be investigated before replacing the TCM.

If the message  Wheel Drive Only.Traction Reduced' appars temporarily and a DT is stored relating to over temperature, the failure is unlikely to be corrected by replacement of the TCCM. Cause of overheat must be investigated.

If the TCCM requires replacement, the procedure detailed in the applicable repair procedure must be followed. Adaptive parameters must be copied from old unit and transferred to the new unit.

The instrument cluster is connected to the TCM via the high speed CAN (controller area network) bus. Transmission status is transmitted by the TCM and displayed to the driver in the instrument cluster. Refer to: Instrument Cluster (413-01 Instrument Cluster, Description and Operation).

The transmission status display is located in the tachometer of the instrument cluster. The display shows the selector lever position or the selected gear when in manual and sport modes.

The following table shows the displays and their descriptions.

![](images/_MISSING_1ca38524b6ed8c62b08ee654e09ec723e600fd657cd725967a5d172e75bf521c.jpg)
The message center i loated in the instrument cluster. The message center is a Thin Film Trasistor (TF) display that relays vehicle status and operating information to the driver and can display messages relating to a number of vehicle systems. If transmission fault occurs, the message GEARBOX FAULT is displayed in the message center. Refer to: Information and Message Center (413-08 Information and Message Center, Description and Operation).

The transmission comprises the main casing which houses allof the transmission components. The main casing also incorporates an integral torque converter housing.

On 2.2L Dw12C models the transmission casing has a foam NVH (noise, vibration and harshness) cover over the torque converter housing.

A fluid pan is attached to the lower face of the main casing and is secured with bolt. The fluid pan is sealed to the main casing with a gasket. Removal ofthe fluid pan allows access to the Mechatronic valve block. The fluid pan has magnets located at the rear which collects any ferrous metallic particles present in the transmission fluid.

Afluid filter is located inside the fluid pan. If the transmission fluid becomes contaminated or after any service work, the flui pan with integral filter must be replaced.

The transmission does not have a Bowden cable for park lock operation.This i initiated electronically when the T is movec to the' park position.Anemergncy park interlock release mechanism i provied t rleasethe park interlck ailure occurs.

A new feature of the 8 speed transmission is decoupling of the transmission when the vehicle is at a standstill. Normallythe transmission remains in gear with the torque converter slipping and the vehicle is prevented from moving by appying the brake.The new system disengages one of the transmisson clutches and only a minimum rotating load remains. This has the effect of further reducing fuel consumption.

The internal oil pump is driven by a simplex chain and 2 drive gears from the torque converter. The oil pump is a double stroke vane cell pump which delivers 50 cm3 of transmission fluid per revolution.

The integral torque converter housing provides protection for the torque converter assembly and also provides the attachment for the gearbox to the engine. The torque converter is a non-serviceable assembly which also contains the lock-up clutch mechanism.

The main casing contains the following major components

Input shaft   
Output shaft Mechatronic valve block which contains the solenoids, speed sensors and the TCM Three rotating multiplate drive clutches Two fixed multiplate brake clutches   
Four planetary gear trains.

Transmission Sectional View

![](images/_MISSING_6e3ed1f96cc0fe5391c6d6e5dfe6464d0f14f73215538ffb6abe4541ff4e4b6c.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_073fdaa676b51ff054f1f978a3400e5e67e95d081099fb3268e272db6e0aa59a.jpg)

The ATF (automatic transmissio fluid) pump is an integral part of the transmission. The ATF pump is used to supply hydraulic pressure for the operation of the control valves and clutches, to pass the fuid trough the transmission cooler and to lubricate the gears and shafts.

The ZF 8HP70 ATF pump is a double stroke, vane type pump and is located below the transmisson input shaft. The pump is driven by a chain drive from a sprocket located on the input shaft. The pump has a delivery rate of 50 cm 3 per revolution. The drive sprocket is driven at engine speed through a splined connection in the torque converter shell.

Double Vane ATF Pump Location

![](images/_MISSING_5effd99b480a981fc66d2c8e3a3cb2e7cab2106299ea63c684fbcd35be5001b8.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_19b96497188d3875f531e01147200c712fdbe73f20383a17a71a8b1cc2a99650.jpg)

The ATF pump comprises a sprocket, a rear cover with bearing, a front cover with bearing, a cylinder, a rotor shaft and a rot with vanes. A pressure relief valve is fited in the pressure outlet gallery from the pump but is not an integral part of the pump itself.

A sprocket is located around the transmission input shaft. Splines on the torque converter nose and the sprocket ensure a positive drive.A simplex chain transmits the rotation of the torque converter cover int rotation of the pump rotor shaft via a second sprocket fitted to the rotor shaft. The gearing of the two sprocket rotates the pump rotor shaft at a speed slightly higher than the Revolutions Per minute (RPM) of the torque converter cover which is directly connected to the engine crank.

The pump contains 7 vanes which are attached to the rotor and rotate within the cam shaped cylinder. As the vanes rotate, the eccentrity of the central hole in the cylinder causes the space between the vanes to increase.This causes a depression between the vanes and fluid is drawn into the space between the vanes via a suction port connected to the fluid pan. The fluid passes through the fluid pan filter before it is drawn into the pump.

As the rotor shaft rotates further, the inlet port is closed by the vanes which have drawn in fluid, trapping the fluid in the space between the vanes. The ecentric hole in the cylinder causes the space between the vanes to decrease and consequentially compresses and pressurizes the fluid trapped between them.

Further rotation of the rotor shaft moves the vanes towards the outlet port. As the vanes pass the outlet port the pressurized fluid passes from the space between the vanes into the pressure gallery to the pressure relief valve.

As the ATF pump is a double stroke vane pump, this sequence is repeated twice per revolution of the rotor shaft.

The pressure relief valve control the pressure and flow of fluid delivered to the transmission valve block, torque converter and other components. Pressure is controlled by a relief valve which limits the maximum system pressure to 32 bar (464 /in. The pressure control maintains a constant pressure of fluid rrespective of torque converter input shaft rotational speed. A metering orifice isubject to the pump output pressure. f the pressurein the orifice reaches a predeterminedlevel, aspring loaded ballin the flw ontrol valve i lited fro its seat and pressurised fluid is allowed to reiulate trough the pump.

### Automatic Transmission/Transaxle - GTDi 2.0L Petrol/TD4 2.2L Diesel/TDV6 3.0L Di


Multiplate Clutch or Brake – Typical

![](images/_MISSING_d9c389739097025e399d15429ff0cc6c5873dc6ca67c2597083477ed53afd693.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_7b529e17e7f376c999a4cc420fc62d38d1f273cbfc7eff06eae44be2126c6bdd.jpg)
There are three drive clutches and two brakes used in the transmission. Each clutch comprises a number of friction plates dependent on the output controlled. A typical clutch consist of a numberof alternating steel plates and plates with friction material bonded to each face.

The clutch plates are held apart mechanicallyby a diaphragm spring and hydraulically by dynamic pressure. The pressure is derived from a lubrication channel which supplies fluid to the bearings and clutch cooling. The fluid is passed via a drling in the input shaf into the chamber between the baffle plate and the piston. To prevent inadvertent clutch appication due to pressure build up produced by centrifugal force, the fluid in the dynamic pressure equalization chamber overcomes any centrifugal pressure in the piston chamber and holds the piston off the clutch plate assembly.

When clutch application is required, main pressure from the fluid pump is applied to the piston chamber from the suppy port. This main pressure overcomes the low pressure fluid present in the dynamic pressure equalization chamber. The piston moves, against the pressure applied by the diaphragm spring, and compresses the clutch plate assembly. When the main pressure falls, the diaphragm spring pushes the piston away from the clutch plate assembly, disengaging the clutch.

The TM is an integral part of the Mechatronic valve block which is located at the bottom of the transmission, within the fluid pan. The TCM is the main controlling component of the transmission.

The TCM processes signals from the transmission speed and temperature sensors, ECM and other vehicle systems. From the received signal inputs and pre-programmed data, the module calculates the correct gear, torque converter clutch seting and optimum pressure settings for gear shift and lock-up clutch control.

The transmission status display is located in the tachometer. The display shows the JaguarDrive TCS position. When the transmission is in the Jaguar sequential shift mode the current gear is displayed in the information window.

The message center is located in the instrument cluster. The message center is a Thin Film Transistor display that relays vehicle status and operating iformation to the driver and can display messages relating to a number of vehicle systems. f a transmission fault occurs, the message GEARBOX FAULT is displayed in the message center. Refer to: Information and Message Center (413-08 Information and Message Center, Description and Operation).

The TM outputs signals to control the shift control solenoid valves and the EPRS's to control the hydraulic operation of the transmission.

The TCM processes signals from the transmission speed and temperature sensors, the TCS , the ECM and other vehicle systems. From the reeived signal inputs and pre-programmed data, the M calculates the correct gear, torque converter clutch setting and optimum pressure settings for gear shift and lock-up clutch control.

The ECM supplies the engine management data over the high speed CAN bus. The TCM requires engine data to eficienty control the trasmission operation, for example;fywheel torque, egine spee, accelerator pedal angle, engine temperature. The steering angle sensor and the ABS (anti-lock brake system) module also supply data to the TM on the high speed CAN bus. The TM uses data from these systems to suspend gear changes when the vehicle is cornering and/or the ABS module is controlling braking or traction control.

The CB (central junction box) supplies steering wheel paddle data over the high speed CAN bus. The TCM uses this to schedule driver requested upshifts and downshifts.

Using the signal inputs and the memorized data, the TCM control program computes the correct gear and torque converter lock-up clutch setting and the optimum pressure setings for gear shift and lock-up clutch control. Special output-side modules (power output stages, current regulator circuits), allow the TM to control the solenoid valves and pressure regulators and consequently precisely control the hydraulics of the automatic transmisson. In addition, the amount and duration of engine interventions are supplied to the engine management by way of the CAN bus.

The TCM determines the position of the TCS using signals from the TCS on the high speed CAN bus and LIN (local interconnect network) bus.

The TCM transmits the position of the TCS and any manual gear selected on the high speed CAN bus. This information is shown in the gear selector display in the instrument cluster.

The transmission comprises the main casing which houses all of the transmission components. The main casing also incorporates an integral torque converter housing.

wo variants of the casing are available to provide for the RWD (rear wheel drive) and the AWD (all-wheel drive) versions of the vehice.The transmission iternals are identical with only the output shaft being different between the two main casing types.

A fluid pan is attached to the lower face of the main casing and is secured with bolt. The fluid pan is sealed to the main casing with a gasket. Removal of the fluid pan allows access to the Mechatronic valve block. The fluid pan has magnets located at the rear which collect any ferrous metallic particles present in the ATF (automatic transmission fluid) .

A fluid fiter is located inside the fluid pan. If the ATF becomes contaminated or after any service work, the fluid pan with integral filter must be replaced.

The transmission does not have a Bowden cable for park lock operation. This i initiated electronically when the S is moved to the 'P' park position. Anemergency park interlock release mechanism is provided to releasethe park interlock if a failure occurs. Refer to: External Controls (307-05A Automatic Transmission/Transaxle External Controls - V8 5.0L Petrol/V8 S/ 5.0l PDiand eg.

A feature of the 8 speed transmission is decoupling of the transmission when the vehicle is at a standstil. Normall the transmission remains in gear with the torque converter slipping and the vehicle is prevented from moving by applying the brake. The new system disengages one of the transmission clutches and only a minimum rotating load remains. This has the effect of further reducing fuel consumption.

The internalfuid pump is driven by a simplex chain and 2 drive gears from the torque converter. The fluid pump is a double stroke vane cell pump which delivers 50 cm3 of ATF per revolution.

The integral torque converter housing provides protection for the torque converter assembly and also provides the attachment for the transmission to the engine.The torque converter is a non-serviceable assembly which also contains the lock-up clutch mechanism.

The main casing contains the following major components

Input shaft   
Output shaft   
Mechatronic valve block which contains the solenoids, speed sensors and the TCM Three rotating multiplate drive clutches   
Two fixed multiplate brake clutches   
Four planetary gear trains.

### Published: 04-Jan-2016 Transmission/Transaxle Cooling - GTDi 2.0L Petrol/TD4 2.2


Description and Operation

Control Diagram

NOTE: A = Hardwired; D = High speed CAN bus; O = LIN bus

CONTROL DIAGRAM

![](images/_MISSING_ba0d701a57ee4fe48198f5ec0ac145229d916cea24afdeeb8c2ac8bb1b34649f.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_47523726289d1304ec9bf364c45c3006bd1346715eec63a8f655c54a0e37dae6.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_6f58e484bcdbf47f63a3735044ef232fcbf6259b175a13eb3192d7a68a89e3f9.jpg)

Rotation of the JaguarDrive TS (transmission control switch to any of the five positions i sensed by the TM (transmission control module) via the high speed CAN (controller area network) bus. A LIN (local interconnect network) bus connection is also provided, but is only used in the event of a CAN bus filure as a back-up. The TM then react according to the selected position. The TCS is a magnetic system using Hall effect sensors to determine the position of the TCS.

The S(sport) position selection allows the TM to operate the transmission using the semi-automatic Jaguar sequential shift. Gear selections are sensed by the TM when the driver operates the steering wheel paddle switches. Once the S position is confirmed, the TCM outputs appropriate iformation on the high speed CAN bus which is received by the instrument cluster to display the gear selection information in the message center. Refer to: Information and Message Center (413-08 Information and Message Center, Description and Operation).

The paddles can also be used on a temporary basis when the TCS is in the D (drive) position to override the automatic gear selection if required.

Two gear change padde' switches are fitted at the rear of thesteering wheel and allow thedriver to operate the transmission as a semi-automatic manual gearbox using the Jaguar sequential shift feature.

Each paddle switch has three connections; ground, ilumination PWM (pulse width modulation) supply and ground switch signal. The padde switches are hardwired to the right steering wheel witchpack. Operation of the paddle witch completes a ground path to the switchpack. The switchpack converts the completed ground signalinto a LIN bus signal which is passed via the clockspring to the CB (central junction box). The C converts the signal into a high speed CAN bus signal to the TCM.

Pullig the left downshift ) paddle provides down changes and pulling the right upshift +) padde provides up changes. The first operation of either paddle, after sport mode is selected, puts the transmission into permanent manual Jaguar sequential shift mode. Rotation of the TCS back to the D position, returns the transmission to conventional automatic operation.

Temporary operation of manual Jaguar sequential shift mode can also be operated with the TCS in the D position. Operation ofeither the upshift or downshift paddles activatesthe manal ode peration.  the S is in D, Jaguar seuential shift wil cancel after a time period or can be cancelled by pressing and holding the + paddle for approximately 1.2 seconds.

The temporary operation of the paddles in the 'D' position is disabled in some markets as a default at delivery. This can be overriden in the instrument cluster menu and the driver can cofigure the paddle peration as'Active in'S' only' or 'Active in 'D' and 'S".

![](images/_MISSING_5d72224c5dd01130703e0d5088941d42cc752976f2bec19a18612d33ac19dea2.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_a82a1d8d99db94c8495729ba0d2164158979cb22a14bcd8bd7a74f773cd69198.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_e3dc59fb0381e7e6f62a26c0b719cce92c972cda3936f52f322ea0b923a8081a.jpg)

If a vehicle requires recovery/transportation, the emergency park release mechanism is used to manul disengage the park lock and engage the transmission in neutral.

The emergency park release mechanism consists of a service tool, supplied as part of the vehicle tool kit, and a cable assembly that is connected to a park interlock lever on the transmission.

The cable assembly terminates in the engine compartment, and is secured, via a locating bracket, on the left side of the supercharger casing.The engine cover requires removal for access. The park interlock lever is attached to the transmission selector shaft.

To release the transmission from Park it is necessary to connect the emergency park release service tool to the cable assembly. When operated, the emergency park release mechanism turns the transmission selector shaft to the neutral position.

Actuation of the emergency park release on AWD vehicles is atwo person peration with the footbrake applied  an assistant is not available, the vehicle must be secured via chocks to prevent against vehicle rlaway. The emergency park release service tool is marked with a visible warning label to the operator that the foot brake must be applied during operation.

To disengage the park lock:

Ensure the vehicle is secured via the footbrake (two people required) or wheel chocks.   
Open the luggage compartment lid and access the vehicle tool kit. Remove the emergency park release service tool.   
Open the hood and remove the engine cover (Refer to the applicable service repair procedure).   
Release the cable from the clip on the supercharger and remove the protective end cap from the cable assembly.   
Attach the emergency park release service too to the cable assembly, ensuring the latches on the connector and the housing are fully engaged.   
Rotate the locking cylinder of the emergency park release lever 90 degrees counterclockwise.   
Pul the operating lever upwards and ensure it locks in the vertical position.

Raising the operating lever causes the emergency park release cable to rotate the park interlock lever on the transmission, which disengages the parking pawl and engages neutral. This allows the vehicle to freewheel.

To re-engage the park lock:

Hold the strap on the operating lever, release the latch and lower the operating lever to the horizontal position Lock the operating lever by turning the locking cylinder 90 degrees clockwise.   
Depressthe latches on the connector and disconnect the emergency park release service too from the housing on the cable assembly.   
Replace the protective end cap on the lower cable, ensuring that the latches engage.   
Ensure the cable is securely located in the bracket on the supercharger.   
Replace the engine cover (Refer to the applicable service repair procedure) and close the hood.   
Replace the emergency park release service tool in the luggage compartment and close the luggage compartment lid.

Published: 12-Sep-2012

The external controls for the transmission consist of a Transmission Control Switch (TCs), two paddle switches and an emergency park release.

The TCS transmits driver transmission selections to the TM (transmission control module). The paddle switches can be used to initiate gear changes, with the S ieither the D or S position, causing a change of operating mode from automati gear selection to manual gear selection. The emergency park release ensures the transmission is kept in neutral during vehicle recovery operations.

On RWD vehicles, the park release operating lever is located below a cover in the floor console. On AWD vehicles, the operating lever is located in the engine compartment, attached to the supercharger on the left side of the engine.

Four additional switches adjacent to the JaguarDrive TCs (transmisson control switch) control the JaguarDrive control functions. Refer to: Ride and Handling Optimization (204-06 Ride and Handling Optimization, Description and Operation) / Anti-Lock Control - Stability Assist (206-09 Anti-Lock Control - Stability Assist, Description and Operation).

Fluid from the ATF (automatic transmission fluid pump in the automatic transmissio flows through the suppy hose and pipe to the transmission fluid cooler.The fluid then flows through the transmission fluid cooler, and the return hose and pipe, to the sump of the automatic transmission.

The transmission fluid coolris a dedicated cooler which is connected into the engine cooling system circuit. The transmission fluid is cooled by the temperature differential between the transmission fluid and the engine coolant flowing through the cooler.

Vehicles with the 2.2L DW12C diesel engine and the 8 speed transmission have a thermostatic valve located in the transmission cooler fluid supply and return lines. The valve contains a spring and wax thermostat which is closed when transmission fluid temperatures are below 69  (156.2FAt temperatures of 69  (156. F and above, the valve begins to open allowing the fluid to flow around the cooler. The valve is fully open at temperatures of 7  (174.2F.

The keylessvehicle module controls signal transmissions to and from the Smart Key and provides authorization to allow the vehicle to be started. The module has a medium speed CAN connection to the CB for authorizing vehicle starting.

The Radio Frequency (RF) receiver transmission is received from the Smart Key to enable key identification.

The message center D (liquid crystal display) display has a viewable area of 126 pixels horizontal and 174 pixels vertical. It is divided into six information display zones as follows, starting from the top:

Set speed   
Transmission position   
Warning /message display   
JaguarDrive Optimization icon   
Odometer/Trip computer information Fuel level.

The message center is active at alltmes when the iition is on and can also be active when the igition is of dependent on the iformation to be displayed.The messge center L illumination icontrolled by the un lad light sensor located on the instrument panel.In bright conditions, the ilumination is set to maximum brightness.As the ambient light levels drop, the illumination dims. When thelights ar itched on or activated by theUTo function, the ilmination perates i the same way until a defined ambient light threshold is reached, at this point the seting of the panelilumination dimmer in the auxiliary light switch will control the brightness.

If more than one message is active, each message is displayed for 4 seconds in the order of priority. Once all messages have been displayed, they are again displayed in turn for 2 seconds each. Warning messages can be displayed when the ignition is in accessory power mode 4 which is the initial ignition state when a door is opened.

The gear position display shows JaguarDrive selector position or selected gear when using the Jaguar Sequential Shift. The gear selector module transmits a CAN message to the instrument cluster for gear selector lever position. The module also outputs a 'not in park' signal to the instrument cluster. The TCM transmits a high speed CAN message to the instrument cluster with data containing the selected gear when in Jaguar Sequential Shift mode.

Component Description

The gear position display shows the JaguarDrive selector position or the selected gear when using the Jaguar Sequential Shift.

The applicable drive letter is highlighted to show that a selection has been made using the JaguarDrive selector.

When Jaguar Sequential Shift is selected, the letters change to numbers; 1 - 6, and the selected gear is highlighted to emphasize the selection to the driver.

The parking aid camera receives an ignition power mode 6 power supply from the RB . It also has a LIN bus connection with the RJB , which is used as a gateway.

A shielded co-axial cable connection between the camera and the TSD is used for the video image transmission.

The camera receives power at alltimes when the ignition is in power mode . When reverse gear is selected, the RJB transmits a reverse selected message on the medium speed CN bus. The information and entertainment module transfers the message on the MOST ring to the TSD, which displays the video input from the parking aid camera in preference to the parking aid alert screen.

The display from the camera incorporates graphic overlays, indicating vehicle direction, width and proximity to surounding objects.

A single touch on the screen wil revert the display to the parking aid alert screen. The camera view can be reselected by pressing the Rear Camera soft key on the TSD.

When reverse gear is deselected, the camera image remains on the TSD for 2 seconds after the transmission has been put into D (drive). If the vehicle forward speed in D exceeds 16 km/h (10 mph) the camera image is removed from the TSD.

Ifthe TD iswitched of the camera image wil be automaticall displayed when reverse gear is selected. When reverse gear is deselected, after 10 seconds the TSD will revert back to its switched off state.

### Restraints Control Module


![](images/_MISSING_309533038762fd34f8ad89f2b91c489ee34e014ba678fa7c72a8df92ab7a1666.jpg)

The RCM is installd on the top of the transmission tunnel, in line with the B pilars, and controls operation of the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS). The main functions of the RCM include:

Crash detection and recording   
Air bag and pretensioner firig   
elf-test and system monitoring, with status indication via the air bag warning lamp and non-volatile storage of fault information.

The RCM determines which elements of the SRS are to be deployed by using two internal areas:

Crash severity evaluation Deployment handler.

Crash severity evaluation evaluates crash severity by using data from the RCM internal accelerometer, the front crash sensor and the safety belt buckle sensor. Based on this data, the RCM decides which level of air bag module deployment is required and forwards the information to the second area, the deployment handler.

The deployment hander evaluates the status of the seat track position sensor and safety belt buckle sensors before a decision is made about which restraints should finally be deployed.

Data from the side crash sensors is used by the RCM in conjunction with acceleration data from the RCM internal accelerometer to make a deployment decision. The RCM processes the accleration data and subject to an impact being of high enough severity, decides whether the side air bag module should be deployed.

On board testing of the air bag modules, front safety belt pretensioner firing circuits, warning indicator circuits and module status (the crash and side impact sensors perform basic self-test) is performed by the RCM toether with the storing of fault codes.

The RCM drives the SRS indicator on the instrument pack via a CAN signal. f the warning lamp fail, a fault code is recorded and a warning tone is sounded in place of the lamp if a further fault occurs. It also provides a temporary back-up power supply to operate the air bag modulesi the event that in crash coditions, the battry supply is lost.  theevent of a crash, it records certain data which can be accessed via the diagnostic connector.

A saving sensor in the RCM provides confirmation of an impact to verify if air bag and pretensioner activation is necessary. Various firing strategies are employed by the RCM to ensure that during an accident only the appropriate air bags and pretensioners are fired. The firing strategy used also depends on the inputs from the safety belt switches and the occupant monitoring system.

An energy reserve in the RCM ensures there is always a minimum of 150 miliseconds of stored energy available if the power supply from the igition switch is disrupted during a crash. The stored energ is sufiient to produce firing signals for the driver air bag, the passenger air bag and the safety belt pretensioners.

When the ignition is switched on theRCM performs a self-test and then performs cyclical monitoring of the system. f a fault is detected the RCM stores a related fault code andiluminates the air bag warning indicator. The faults can be retrieved by the recommended Jaguar dianostic tol ver the AN bus. If a fault that could cuse a false fire signal is detected, the RCM disables the respective firing circuit, and keeps it disabled during a crash event.
